contentType.other: This paper draws on my experience in operating model design.

detail.abstract: Over twenty-five years of designing, building, and scaling operating models across shared services, Global Business Services (GBS), and Global Capability Centres (GCCs) I have learned that transformation succeeds or fails long before the first process is migrated. It is decided in how leaders frame the ambition, sequence the change, and manage the human system that must carry it. This paper distils the practical lessons of that experience: why organizations consistently underestimate governance and culture while over-engineering structure and technology; why the most common failure mode is treating an operating model as an org chart rather than a system of decisions, work, and accountability; and why AI is now forcing the most consequential redesign in a generation. I argue that future-ready operating models will be defined less by where work sits and more by how quickly organizations can reconfigure work itself. The executives who win the next decade will build modular structures, outcome-based governance, AI-fluent talent, and a culture that treats change as a permanent capability rather than a project. The paper closes with candid advice for leaders taking on transformation mandates.

title: The Legal Impact of Digital Data Exchange on Competition in European Union Container Ports

detail.title: The Legal Impact of Digital Data Exchange on Competition in European Union Container Ports
detail.abstract: Container port competition increasingly depends on the systems through which operational instructions, cargo statuses, access permissions, and event records circulate. Physical capacity may remain contestable while one undertaking controls the data required to use that capacity, switch providers, or verify performance. This article connects the economic structure of European container ports with the law governing market definition, horizontal cooperation, abuse of dominance, data access, electronic freight information, and maritime reporting. It argues that primary operational data become a source of market power when control over their creation, timing, format, transfer, or correction enables an undertaking to restrict participation or shape the legally significant history of operations. The proposed model separates operational coordination from commercial surveillance and combines non-discriminatory access with purpose limitation, structured portability, preservation of original records, and independent oversight.

title: Extending Arbitration Agreements to Non-signatories: A Defence of the Group of Companies Doctrine

detail.title: Extending Arbitration Agreements to Non-signatories: A Defence of the Group of Companies Doctrine
detail.abstract: Consent is the cornerstone of international arbitration. Since arbitration entails a waiver of the right to seek recourse from courts, the concept rests fundamentally on consent and operates on the principle of party autonomy. The intention of the parties to arbitrate manifests in the form of an arbitration agreement. However, on occasion, the scope of an arbitration agreement is extended to non-signatories when it is difficult or ineffective to resolve the dispute without the particular party being part of the proceedings. In this context, a mechanism often relied upon is the Group of Companies Doctrine (“the Doctrine”), which prescribes a threefold test to determine whether the non-signatory is bound by the arbitration agreement. Tribunals check for the existence of a tight group structure, involvement of the third party in the conclusion of the contract, and common intention of all parties to bind the third party to the arbitration agreement. The article constructs a defence of the doctrine by addressing claims against its validity. It attempts to prove that consent can be manifested through written agreement as well as through the behaviour of parties. It is this behaviour that the doctrine inquires into, thus upholding arbitration’s core tenet of consent.

title: When Does Foreign Technology Help Firms from Periphery Countries Improve Their Environmental Impact? An Ability-Motivation-Opportunity Framework

detail.title: When Does Foreign Technology Help Firms from Periphery Countries Improve Their Environmental Impact? An Ability-Motivation-Opportunity Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no potential conflicts of interest with respect to the research, authorship, and/or publication of this article

detail.abstract: In the face of climate change, transferring climate-friendly technologies to peripheral countries, where firms often rely on outdated technologies, poses a significant policy challenge. Licensing foreign technology to these firms offers promise, yet uncertainties remain regarding how they implement such technologies and consequently improve their environmental performance. This study develops an ability-motivation-opportunity framework to capture the interplay between firms’ technical capabilities, internal motivational forces, and external opportunity structures in institutionally underdeveloped settings. Analyzing a sample of 2,237 firms from 30 countries in Eastern Europe and Central Asia, the findings indicate that firms acquiring licensed foreign technology adopt more environmentally friendly measures. However, the extent of these improvements is jointly determined by their technical ability, both intrinsic and extrinsic motivations, and the opportunity to devote resources and attention to these measures. The results highlight that policy efforts to reduce emissions must go beyond merely facilitating technology licensing. Effective strategies ideally also focus on enhancing firms’ internal capabilities, strengthening incentives to fully exploit new technology features, and streamlining administrative procedures that hinder the adoption of cleaner production practices.

title: Locally Valid Dantzig-Wolfe Optimality Cuts for Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
affiliations: and School of Business and Management, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Locally Valid Dantzig-Wolfe Optimality Cuts for Stochastic Mixed-Integer Programs
detail.abstract: We study Dantzig-Wolfe (DW) optimality cuts for two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs with mixed-integer recourse. The second-stage integrality generally induces discontinuous recourse value functions, making the construction of strong approximations a central challenge for decomposition algorithms. Benders cuts are inexpensive to generate but often weak because they are derived from the linear-programming relaxation. Lagrangian cuts can yield stronger approximations, but their generation often requires repeatedly solving mixed-integer subproblems. We address this strength-cost trade-off by deriving optimality cuts from a DW relaxation of the recourse problem. These cuts provide strong approximations and enable the accumulation and reuse of mixed-integer subproblem information across cut-generation iterations. We further show that a facet-defining cut can be obtained directly from the DW relaxation, without solving an auxiliary cut-selection problem. We then introduce locally valid optimality cuts, which are valid only on regions certified to contain all optimal first-stage solutions, and use state-screening updates to maintain these regions safely. Finally, we embed these cuts into a spatial branch-and-bound framework and prove global convergence. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can improve algorithm performance, and a study of stochastic air-ground service network design using real-world data further illustrates its practical relevance.

title: Bayesian Networks for Financial Risk Management: An Illustrative Implementation with pgmpy

detail.title: Bayesian Networks for Financial Risk Management: An Illustrative Implementation with pgmpy

detail.abstract: Traditional financial risk models such as Value-at-Risk and logistic regression rely heavily on independence and distributional assumptions that often fail during systemic stress. This paper proposes Bayesian Networks (BNs) as a causal and probabilistic alternative for modeling financial risk. BNs explicitly represent dependencies between risk drivers and allow for real-time updating of risk probabilities given new evidence, making them well-suited for regulatory stress testing and explainable AI in finance. We provide a complete technical implementation using pgmpy, an open-source Python library for probabilistic graphical models. First, we construct a BN for credit default risk with nodes for borrower Income, Debt-to-Income ratio, Unemployment, and Default. We demonstrate exact inference via variable elimination and scenario analysis via rejection sampling. Second, we extend the analysis to a real dataset using a 10,000 loan sample from LendingClub 2018 data. We use structure learning with Hill Climbing and parameter estimation with Maximum Likelihood to learn the network from data. The learned model achieves better calibration on out-of-sample default prediction than a baseline logistic regression, and enables counterfactual queries such as P (Def ault|DT I > 40%, U nemployment = High). The results show that BNs offer two key advantages for risk managers: 1) causal interpretability for root-cause analysis, and 2) flexible scenario testing without reestimating the entire model. We discuss implementation challenges including data requirements, scalability, and validation. This work contributes a practical, reproducible framework for deploying BNs in financial institutions and provides all code for replication. The approach is directly applicable to Basel III/IV stress testing, IFRS 9 Expected Credit Loss, and operational risk modeling.

title: Bricolage Governance Under Institutional Voids: From Relational Workaround to Organizational Capability in Moroccan Smes
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: This article examines how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) secure exchange when formal institutions are costly, slow, or practically inaccessible. It argues that organizational bricolage operates not only as a response to resource scarcity but as an alternative governance mechanism, and it specifies the conditions under which this mechanism consolidates into a durable capability. The study uses an interpretivist, abductive, multi-case design covering seven SMEs and two external experts in the Rabat-Salé-Kénitra region of Morocco. Data were generated through a self-administered open-ended written instrument and analysed by abductive thematic coding against eight constructs, with cross-case positioning on the six criteria of a Type A / Type B grid. Bricolage governance appears in every case yet takes two structurally distinct forms: constrained bricolage is reactive, person-dependent, and weakly routinized; strategic bricolage is deliberate, transmissible, and resilient to relational shocks. Four mechanisms recur (partner selection, dispute resolution, informal financing, and practice transmission), and transmission most sharply separates fragile from consolidated configurations. The corpus supports a configurational rather than linear reading: four conditions (environmental, cognitive, organizational, dynamic) are non-substitutable, and each maps onto a qualitatively distinct blockage regime. Within the organizational condition, procedural and informational objectification are jointly necessary, and incentive alignment is the mechanism through which the informational stratum becomes independent of the individuals who carry it. A deviant case documents that the trajectory is reversible when governance capital remains personified. Seven cases do not validate a configurational model at Ragin's standard; the model is offered as an analytic framework rather than as proof. The single-region scope, the survivor composition of the corpus, the collinearity of the conditions with firm tenure, and the written instrument bound the conclusions to conditions of governance efficacy rather than survival. The article reframes relational governance under institutional failure as a constructed, transmissible organizational competence, and reconceptualizes the scalability threshold as an endogenous property of the firm's informational architecture rather than an exogenous size effect.

title: Optimal Size of Government and Economic Growth in Nepal
affiliations: Tribhuvan University

detail.title: Optimal Size of Government and Economic Growth in Nepal

declarations.funderStatement: Research and Educational Development Project Management Committee (RMC) Ratna Rajyalaxmi Campus, Tribhuvan University Kathmandu, Nepal

detail.abstract:
The role of government in developing nations is essential in the contemporary world. Since the end of the post-Washington Consensus, the role of government has been redefined to foster a market economy and improve institutional quality so that economic development can be stimulated. Thus, the optimal size of an economy is crucial to economic development. In this regard, the current study analyses the effects of the optimal size of government on the economic growth of Nepal, using annual time series data from 1976 to 2024 that covers three political regimes—the Panchayat regime, the Multiparty Democracy regime, and the Federal Democratic Republic regime. This study is based on the theories presented by Armey (1995) and Scully (1994). According to their theories, there exists an inverted-U relationship between government expenditure as a proportion of GDP and economic growth. Five successive augmented models have been used for this analysis, considering government expenditure in linear and quadratic forms along with other control variables such as labor force, gross fixed capital formation, and trade openness. The unit root tests conducted using different approaches: Phillips-Perron test, Augmented Dickey-Fuller test, Kwiatkowski-Phillips-Schmidt-Shin test, Zivot-Andrews test, and Fourier Augmented Dickey-Fuller test show that I(1) is dominant in all the study variables but have a mixed order of integration.

Through Fourier approximation, the Fourier Augmented Auto-Regressive Distributed Lag Model (FARDL), which can capture the structural breaks that arise due to various regimes in Nepal and macroeconomic shocks, strongly supports the existence of cointegration between government expenditure and economic growth for all five models with the inclusion of different control variables at the 1% level of significance. The long-run estimates of the FARDL approach yield positive and significant linear coefficients on expenditure (1.237 to 1.970) and negative and significant quadratic coefficients on expenditure (-0.024 to -0.042). The estimation of the optimal level of government, G* = -β1/2β2, remains consistent across all five estimations and comes up to 23.26% to 27.64% of GDP, with an average value of around 25%, and the most comprehensive equation gives G* = 27.64%. Comparing the level of Nepal's expenditure/GDP ratio with the benchmark of the optimal level of government illustrates that the country remained within the growth-promoting region of the Armey curve during both the Panchayat system and the multiparty democracy periods until exceeding its limit starting from 2016–2017 and achieving the highest recorded level of 31.46% in 2018. As for the control variables, trade openness positively and significantly influences economic growth in the long run, while the working population becomes negative in the most elaborate estimation due to Nepal's experience of the labor migration paradox, where a growing number of workers have gone abroad rather than been absorbed domestically.

The conclusions have significant implications for policymaking: The path Nepal follows towards its empirically-derived optimal level of fiscal expansion (spending) within 25% to 27.64% of its GDP, attained through reform of its public expenditure composition, tax collection, and federal fiscal structure, is the evidence-backed fiscal solution required to get back on track for maximizing public expenditures.

title: Cooperation in Service Systems with Strategic Customers
affiliations: , University of Science and Technology of China, Nankai Business School, Nankai University and City University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Cooperation in Service Systems with Strategic Customers
detail.abstract: Cooperation among independent service systems is an important strategy for coping with rising customer delays and demand variability. Classical cooperative queueing models typically assume that customer arrivals are fixed and do not respond to system performance. However, in many modern service settings, customers are sensitive to waiting times and decide whether to join the queue based on expected delays. This demand response can significantly affect the incentives for cooperation. We develop a cooperative queueing framework that incorporates strategic customer behavior. Under fixed capacity, we show that cooperation may become unstable when some firms face high demand relative to their service capacity, in contrast to seminal studies that predict stable cooperation. When firms can adjust capacity, we find that the game becomes convex and fair allocations exist. When firms also make pricing decisions, cooperation remains stable even though convexity may no longer hold. These results differ substantially from those of models that ignore customer response. Our findings suggest that managers should account for customer sensitivity to delays when forming cooperative agreements. Ignoring such behavior can lead to overly optimistic conclusions about the benefits of cooperation. The results also show that allowing flexibility in capacity or pricing decisions can sustain stable cooperation. This provides practical guidance for designing collaboration mechanisms in service systems such as call centers, healthcare operations, and shared service platforms.

title:
Beyond Linear Decision Rules: 
LLM-guided Representation Discovery for Data-driven Optimization
affiliations: Northwestern Polytechnical University, Northwestern Polytechnical University, National University of Singapore (NUS) - Institute of Operations Research and Analytics and

detail.title:
Beyond Linear Decision Rules: 
LLM-guided Representation Discovery for Data-driven Optimization
detail.abstract: Stochastic optimization often restricts recourse decisions to affine parameterizations for computational tractability, potentially creating a substantial and irreducible approximation gap. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to discover richer problem-specific structures that can help narrow this gap. We propose Generative Stochastic Optimization (GenSO), a framework that uses LLMs to discover representations for adaptive recourse while preserving the rigor and tractability of optimization models. The key component of GenSO is the Generative Linear Decision Rule (GenLDR), in which recourse decisions are expressed as linear combinations of closed-form nonlinear basis functions generated by LLMs from problem structure and domain knowledge. Consequently, GenSO increases the expressiveness of recourse decisions without compromising tractability and interpretability. We establish finite-sample guarantees for fixed generated representations and further derive a performance bound under the assumption motivated by empirical scaling laws of LLMs. We evaluate GenSO on a multi-period newsvendor problem and a data center location problem with multi-period job scheduling calibrated using real-world datasets. Across both settings, GenSO consistently outperforms existing benchmarks in out-of-sample evaluations while uncovering interpretable nonlinear decision structures that are difficult to identify through conventional manual design.

title: Beyond Directional Accuracy: Auditing Archived GPT-4 Forecasts for Behavioral Intervention Choice

detail.title: Beyond Directional Accuracy: Auditing Archived GPT-4 Forecasts for Behavioral Intervention Choice

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was a secondary analysis of publicly available, de-identified research archives. It involved no new participant recruitment, contact, intervention, or access to identifiable private information. Therefore, no additional institutional ethics approval or informed consent was required for this secondary analysis. detail.abstract: Behavioral interventions are often selected before their effects are known, but directional accuracy may add little information for that choice. We audited archived forecasts against progressively stronger baselines and evaluated rankings using comparator-identified, winnerselection-adjusted regret. Across 12 dependent probability-frame contrasts nested in four topics, GPT-4 and an arbitrarily small direction-only rule matched every randomized pointestimate sign. GPT-4 nevertheless had mean absolute error of 0.132, compared with 0.086 for the direction-only rule and 0.038 for a leave-one-topic-out common-effect rule, and it did not recover the observed four-topic ordering. In a separate archive of 51 outcomes from eight study clusters, normalized posterior expected offline screening regret was 1.039 for the mean individual-expert rule, 0.988 for a matched-set crowd mean, and 0.755 for GPT-4. Equal-rank combinations had regret of 0.878 with individual forecasts and 0.915 with crowd forecasts. Pairwise posterior comparisons did not support lower regret for either combination than for GPT-4. Winner-selection adjustment raised GPT-4 regret from an observed-winner plug-in value of 0.651 to 0.755. A flat/no-shrinkage model preserved the posterior-mean ordering; imposed dependence widened intervals without supporting an incremental combination advantage. These fixed-archive results do not establish model-general performance, human-AI synergy, welfare gains, or autonomous intervention value.

title: CEO Formative Exposure and Executive Labor Allocation: Evidence from Corporate Gender Inequality
affiliations: Shenzhen University, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Finance, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Finance and University of Macau - Department of Finance and Business Economics

detail.title: CEO Formative Exposure and Executive Labor Allocation: Evidence from Corporate Gender Inequality
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether CEOs' formative social environments affect executive labor allocation in public firms. We study women's access to senior executive authority, where promotion, compensation, and role assignment are personnel decisions boards monitor but cannot fully contract over. Linking hand-collected data on CEOs' birth states and cohorts to historical state-level organizations associated with gender-role liberalization, we find that firms led by high-exposure CEOs have a 4.45-percentage-point lower share of women in top management, relative to a mean of 9.2%, and a 4.11-percentage-point lower representation of women among the five highest-paid executives. The relation is concentrated among male CEOs; for female CEOs, the sign reverses. Evidence around MeToo, CEO turnovers, placebo outcomes, randomized birth-state assignments, and governance heterogeneity is more consistent with a gender-norm imprinting interpretation than with fixed firm culture, regional ideology, or ESG preferences alone. Mechanism tests point to higher credential thresholds, role sorting away from core operating positions, weaker diversity policies, wider pay gaps, and greater litigationrelated disclosure language. The relation is stronger where governance constraints are weaker. Formative environments can shape executive labor allocation and create governance-relevant agency costs when managerial talent is misallocated.

title: To Know or Not to Know? Validating a Chinese Measure of Information Preferences
affiliations: , Academia Sinica - Institute of Political Science, Northwestern University, , National Taiwan Normal University and Carnegie Mellon University - Department of Social and Decision Sciences

detail.title: To Know or Not to Know? Validating a Chinese Measure of Information Preferences
detail.abstract: The Information Preferences Scale (IPS) measures individuals' tendency to seek or avoid potentially useful but unpleasant information. Although the IPS has been validated in English-speaking Western samples, its use in Mandarin-speaking populations has been limited by the absence of a validated Chinese version. We translated the IPS into Traditional Chinese and evaluated its psychometric properties in Mandarinspeaking samples from Taiwan and Hong Kong (N = 1,465). Across studies, the Chinese IPS showed acceptable internal consistency, replicated the theorized multidimensional structure of the original scale, and demonstrated measurement invariance across cultures and languages. In a bilingual Hong Kong sample, IPS scores were moderately stable across English and Chinese administrations, and both versions predicted participants'willingness to learn potentially unflattering peer feedback. We further illustrate the scale's utility by showing domain-specific cultural differences in information preferences. By providing a validated Chinese version of the IPS and evidence of cross-language and cross-cultural comparability, this research enables future studies to examine information seeking and avoidance in Mandarin-speaking populations and to make more defensible cross-cultural comparisons of information preferences.

title: Digital Technologies for Strategic Financial Control: A Review of Concepts, Applications, and Emerging Challenges
affiliations: University of Calabar- Department of Banking & Finance and University of Calabar, Calabar Nigeria

detail.title: Digital Technologies for Strategic Financial Control: A Review of Concepts, Applications, and Emerging Challenges
detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of digital technologies in strengthening strategic financial control within organizations, with particular attention to the banking sector in Nigeria. It conceptualizes digital technologies for strategic financial control as the integration of computer-based systems, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, big data analytics, blockchain, robotic process automation, and enterprise resource planning systems into financial management processes to support budgeting, forecasting, reporting, auditing, risk management, and strategic decision-making. Drawing on existing literature and illustrative case evidence from institutions such as Access Bank, GTBank, JPMorgan Chase, and Amazon, the paper discusses the core components, methods, and applications of these technologies, and highlights their benefits, including improved accuracy, enhanced decision-making, cost reduction, and stronger fraud detection. It also identifies key challenges to adoption, notably cybersecurity risks, high implementation costs, skills gaps, data privacy concerns, and operational vulnerabilities, alongside the regulatory and ethical considerations such as data protection, IFRS compliance, anti-money laundering, and Know-Your-Customer requirements, that govern their use. The paper concludes that while digital technologies have fundamentally reshaped strategic financial control by enabling real-time monitoring and more informed decision-making, realizing their full value requires sustained investment in cybersecurity, continuous staff training, and strong corporate governance. Recommendations are offered for organizations and policymakers seeking to strengthen digital-enabled financial control systems.

title: The Sovereignty Cliff
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley

detail.title: The Sovereignty Cliff
detail.abstract: When a government delegates the operation of critical infrastructure, two processes begin at once: dependency on the operator accumulates, and the government's capacity to measure that dependency decays. We model the joint process. A government prices its relationship with an operator on the perceived feasibility of replacement, observes its dependency through a signal whose precision decays under delegation, and holds a model of the world that omits one term, the operator's strategic investment in irreversibility. The government's total learning over an infinite horizon is finite, and no test run on its routine data can detect the misspecification: the evidence grows linearly while the noise through which it must be heard grows geometrically. The government therefore continues delegating, rationally, after replacement has become infeasible. A revelation event, a crisis, an audit, a failed override, produces a sovereignty cliff, a discontinuous collapse of the government's bargaining position with no change in the underlying state, and the cliff is certain: absent shocks, the government's own belated diligence supplies the revelation. Positive investment in irreversibility is equilibrium behavior for an ordinary profit maximizer, front-loaded in the life of the delegation. Mandated periodic measurement restores what delegation destroys, but must be constitutionally committed, because under the government's own coherent beliefs it will never seem worth its cost, and under a rule that works, almost every audit will look, in hindsight, unnecessary.

title: Evolution (by Periods) of Public Debt in the Republic of Moldova
affiliations: Academy of Economic Studies of Moldova - Faculty of Finance

detail.title: Evolution (by Periods) of Public Debt in the Republic of Moldova

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research did not involve human subjects or interventions; thus, ethical approval was unnecessary.
declarations.funderStatement: The author did not receive any funding for this research.

detail.abstract: The evolution of public debt is a critical indicator of a country's economic and financial health, particularly for the Republic of Moldova, which has a complex socio-political history and an economy in transition. This paper aims to analyze the trends in public debt in the period 1995-2023 within the Republic of Moldova, emphasizing its implications for fiscal responsibility, governance, and economic resilience. Effective management of public debt is essential for sustaining economic growth and addressing urgent societal needs such as infrastructure, healthcare, and education. By examining historical data on public debt, this research will assess its impact on the Republic of Moldova's economic stability and resilience against shocks, which is vital for maintaining investor confidence. Additionally, the findings will provide policymakers with insights to formulate informed fiscal strategies that balance social welfare demands with economic development objectives. The study will also explore how Moldova's public debt dynamics influence relationships with foreign investors and financial institutions, affecting credit ratings and investment decisions in the middle of increasing fiscal pressures from global challenges like economic crises and the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic. Through a comprehensive analysis of public debt evolution across distinct historical periods, this research seeks to enhance understanding of the Republic of Moldova's fiscal landscape and offer recommendations for improved debt management practices.

title: Disinflation Faster than Expected: Transitional Household Credit Risk in Argentina (2016-2026)

detail.title: Disinflation Faster than Expected: Transitional Household Credit Risk in Argentina (2016-2026)
detail.abstract: Rapid disinflation can increase household credit risk by raising the real burden of fixed-rate debt. Using a monthly, product-level panel for Argentina, this paper studies the effect on household credit risk of the disinflation that began after December 2023, when inflation fell from 25% to under 2% within a year. Because non-performing loan (NPL) ratios are highly persistent, responses are estimated with Local Projections on cumulative changes rather than levels. The response is hump-shaped, peaking around 16 months in unsecured, fixed-rate consumer credit, with the aggregate household NPL ratio rising from 2.8% to 12.1%. The findings are consistent with a Fisherian mecha nism: ex-post real lending rates, which move with the gap between contracted nominal rates and realized inflation, shifted from deeply negative — as high and accelerating inflation had been eroding the real value of fixed-rate debt for several years, foster ing a widespread habit of debt dilution among agents — to significantly positive, as disinflation turned out faster than expected.

title: Viral Valuation: Does Online Attention Predict Equity Trading Volume?

detail.title: Viral Valuation: Does Online Attention Predict Equity Trading Volume?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I declare that I have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

detail.abstract: How does online buzz translate into actual stock trades? This paper examines the lead-lag relationship between retail investor attention-proxied by search volume index data-and subsequent trading volumes. Analyzing a six-month dataset of three retail-driven equities (GM E, T SLA, RDDT) and two traditional control stocks (JN J, P G), we calculate Pearson correlation coefficients (r) across three horizons: concurrent (T 0), one-day lag (T + 1), and two-day lag (T + 2). Our analysis shows that while all five stocks see immediate volume spikes on high-attention days (r > 0.70), only the retail-heavy equities maintain a predictive correlation twenty-four hours later (r ≈ 0.35 to 0.41). For our control stocks, this forwardlooking relationship collapses immediately (r ≤ 0.19). To ensure statistical robustness, we construct an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) regression model to control for historical volume autocorrelation. The results suggest that social media hype serves as a reliable shortterm leading indicator of trading activity specifically for speculative retail assets, highlighting a distinct informational bottleneck in how retail investors process information and execute trades.

title: United States Military Actions against Venezuela: Will International Criminal Law be Enforced?

detail.title: United States Military Actions against Venezuela: Will International Criminal Law be Enforced?
detail.abstract: This article is part of a series from expert contributors to address fundamental legal and normative questions arising from the escalating military campaign, including those relating to the role of the law of armed conflict and the law of the sea, as well as the role of senior military lawyers and legal ethics. The series also addresses Article II powers, presidential immunity, government transparency, and the strong presumption of legality for orders under existing law.

title: Polynomial Model Selection with Small Samples: Fitting, Generalization, and Cross-validation in the Analysis of International Tourism in Nicaragua (2020-2024)
affiliations: Keiser University and

detail.title: Polynomial Model Selection with Small Samples: Fitting, Generalization, and Cross-validation in the Analysis of International Tourism in Nicaragua (2020-2024)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflict of interest. This work received no external funding and was conducted exclusively for academic and methodological purposes.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study used publicly available aggregated tourism data with no human or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This study addresses model selection in data-scarce regimes using five annual observations of international tourism arrivals in Nicaragua (2020-2024). Four candidate specifications (linear, quadratic, cubic, and exponential) are fitted and evaluated via leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV), the PRESS statistic, and the corrected AIC c. The results demonstrate that R 2 is a severely biased proxy for predictive performance when p/n ≥ 0.4. The cubic model (R 2 = 0.971) exhibits an out-of-sample prediction error six times larger than that of the linear model (PRESS = 2.61 × 10 6 vs. 4.31 × 10 5) and yields physically impossible forecasts. All criteria converge on the linear model as the optimal specification. Projections for 2025-2030 with 95% parametric bootstrap intervals are provided, together with a fully reproducible Python pipeline.

title: Grifting

detail.title: Grifting
detail.abstract: Many allocations precede reliable evidence about productivity, allowing low-productivity agents to profit by imitating high productivity. This paper studies signaling when an exposed low type can abandon an adverse record and return under a new identity. Successful resetters pool with genuine entrants, so the composition of provisional identities is determined by a renewal fixed point. With exogenous entry, equilibrium is unique. Record linkage breaks renewal chains but can increase first-time imitation by improving trust. Verification has two opposing effects: it directly deters founders and shortens each identity spell, but it also accelerates exposure and successor production. In an automatic-reconstruction benchmark, trust falls exactly when the semielasticity of expected identity-dynasty length exceeds the semielasticity of founder entry; under a constant-elasticity appearance-cost distribution, this comparison yields an explicit linkage threshold governing the sign of verification. With positive reconstruction costs, the same reversal occurs on an open set of primitives. Identity reset also imposes an informational dilution externality on genuine entrants and receivers.

title: Cross-Border Cooperation Among Securities Regulators and Supply Chain Collaboration： Evidence from U.S.-Listed Foreign Firms
affiliations: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Hong Kong Polytechnic University and Xiamen University

detail.title: Cross-Border Cooperation Among Securities Regulators and Supply Chain Collaboration： Evidence from U.S.-Listed Foreign Firms
detail.abstract: International supply chains are essential for linking global markets but face persistent challenges. While regulatory frameworks are crucial for supporting international business operations, fragmented oversight across jurisdictions often undermines supply chain resilience. We examine how cooperation among securities regulators, through the adoption of the Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU), affects global supply chain contracting. Using a stacked difference-indifferences model, we find that relative to domestic firms, foreign firms listed in the U.S. experience increases in both new contracts and new customers from MMoU signatory countries after their home countries sign the agreement. This positive effect is more pronounced among firms facing higher agency costs, and tighter financial constraints, as well as in countries with greater barriers to contract enforcement. The MMoU strengthens suppliers' financing capacity and lengthens supply chain relationship and contract durations. We further show that the expansion in supply chain contracting is driven primarily by customers from non-U.S. MMoU member countries. Overall, our findings demonstrate that cross-border regulatory cooperation generates positive spillovers in fostering global supply chains.

title: RED-REJECT-2026-v1: A 96-Day Public Corpus of Algorithmic Filter Rejections with Post-Rejection Follow-up Samples on the Solana pump.fun Ecosystem

detail.title: RED-REJECT-2026-v1: A 96-Day Public Corpus of Algorithmic Filter Rejections with Post-Rejection Follow-up Samples on the Solana pump.fun Ecosystem
detail.abstract: Public empirical research on algorithmic trading in decentralised memecoin markets is constrained by data: authors typically release small labelled subsets of their internal corpora, if anything at all, and reproducibility beyond the specific analyses reported is rarely supported. We release RED-REJECT-2026-v1, a 96-day continuous public corpus of every algorithmic filter rejection recorded by a live paper-trading fleet on the Solana pump.fun ecosystem, together with post-rejection follow-up price, liquidity, and volume samples at repeated horizons. The corpus contains 716,762 sample records across 4,635 unique SPL token mints, spanning 2026-04-11 to 2026-07-16. Eight named filter families are represented (downtrend_24h, marketcap_out_of_range, multi_tf_fade, timeSlot_not_strong, hour_blacklist, ultra_fast_reject_exit, utc_hour_blocked, h6_sellers_dominating), with 348 rows (0.05 percent) carrying a null rejection reason. Four primary DEX venues account for over 98 percent of coverage (pumpswap 91.8 percent, meteora 2.7 percent, raydium 2.5 percent, pumpfun 1.8 percent); a small residual of 8,505 rows carries metadao or unknown venue identifiers. Later rows also carry BTC macro-regime context (fear-greed index, regime label). The corpus operationalises the Post-Rejection Follow-up Sampling (PRFS) methodology (Kamat 2026a) at production scale, and is the underlying data for a family of published papers on rejection-outcomeclassified precision auditing (Kamat 2026b), a smaller labelled benchmark subset (Kamat 2026c, RED-2400), a filter-ablation empirical application (Kamat 2026d), and a two-window lifecycle-stage separation analysis (Kamat 2026e). All data are released under CC-BY-4.0 with a byte-exact SHA-256 manifest for reproducibility.

title: Results-Oriented Culture and SEC Enforcement
affiliations: Boston College, City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - College of Business and

detail.title: Results-Oriented Culture and SEC Enforcement
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how a results-oriented organizational culture, which focuses on achievements and emphasizes competition, influences the enforcement activity at the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Using an internal survey with a response rate of nearly 60%, we develop a novel measure of results-orientation and show that SEC staff are more likely to initiate investigations when they perceive their office as being more results-oriented. However, this association is primarily observed for “easier” cases, and investigations opened by results-oriented offices are less likely to lead to subsequent enforcement actions. Despite this, firms located in the jurisdiction of a results-oriented office exhibit fewer financial reporting irregularities overall, suggesting that results-oriented offices are still more effective at deterring financial reporting misconduct compared to offices that are less results-oriented. Taken together, our results provide a first glimpse into how organizational culture influences the effectiveness of public-sector agencies.

title: Are All Patents Equal? How Patent Attributes Shape Market Reactions to Family and Nonfamily Firm Innovation
affiliations: , Jonkoping University - Jonkoping International Business School (JIBS), Macquarie University, Macquarie Business School and Villanova University - School of Business

detail.title: Are All Patents Equal? How Patent Attributes Shape Market Reactions to Family and Nonfamily Firm Innovation
detail.abstract: Integrating family firm innovation research with signaling theory, we develop a framework explaining market reactions to patents granted to family versus nonfamily firms. Using a U.S. dataset of 52,241 patents from 2014-2018, we find the stock market reacts more positively to patents granted to family firms than nonfamily firms. We then examine reactions to radical versus incremental patents. Patents reflecting radical innovation, measured by novelty and pedigree, create greater market value for family firms than nonfamily firms, although the pedigree effect is only marginally significant. By contrast, patents reflecting incremental innovation, measured by temporal depth, have little effect on nonfamily firms' market value but reduce family firms' market value.

title: The Standing Gap: An Accountability Gap that Survives Transparency

detail.title: The Standing Gap: An Accountability Gap that Survives Transparency
detail.abstract: Professional conclusions warrant reliance partly because they are formed within institutions that place a licence, reputation, legal position, and disciplinary identity at stake. AI can separate that standing-bearing position from the production of the judgment while leaving a human firm's signature and liability intact. This paper calls the separation standing displacement and the uncovered production-side residue the standing gap. It identifies two coupled mechanisms: load-bearing judgment formation moves to a node without actor-side professional standing, while formal responsibility remains attached to, or is re-attached to, a standing-bearing organization at deployment. A full-transparency test distinguishes this gap from failures of control, attribution, or epistemic access: making an AI deterministic and reconstructable improves supervision and answerability but does not itself give the system a licence, professional reputation, or disciplinary position. The claim is limited to operative AI contributions to relied-on professional judgments unless substantively absorbed through task-level human judgment. Substantive absorption can reduce or eliminate the uncovered residue, but it requires nontrivial task-level professional work rather than plausibility review. A vacancy need not be material. An independent-expert workflow illustrates the separation across five institutional nodes. The paper supplies a diagnostic object, not a measure, universal threshold, or remedy.

title: Withering on the Vine: A Formal Theory of Modern Hiring Practices and Labor Market Failures

detail.title: Withering on the Vine: A Formal Theory of Modern Hiring Practices and Labor Market Failures

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests that could have influenced this research.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This article uses a theoretical model, and did not involve human subjects; therefore, ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic model of job search in which hiring experiences can alter the applicant state from which subsequent search is conducted. The worker’s state includes liquid assets, beliefs about application success, accumulated negative hiring experience, and psychological search capital governing how effectively raw effort is converted into hiring outcomes. Rejection, employer nonresponse, prolonged screening, repeated assessments, and other unrewarded demands deplete search capital, raise application costs, and reduce perceived returns to search. Declining assets also increase financial pressure, lowering search effectiveness before the borrowing constraint binds. These mechanisms generate applicant-side negative state dependence in the optimized job-finding hazard even when worker productivity and the vacancy distribution remain unchanged. They may also redirect search away from identity-relevant and, under an additional alignment condition, higher-match vacancies. Financial depletion lowers the reservation job value and may induce acceptance of poorly matched employment, entry into hiring-bypass work, or non participation. If accepted employment is sufficiently burdensome, reduced on-the-job search capacity can make mismatch persistent. Because firms need not internalize how screening burdens affect applicants’ subsequent search elsewhere, individually rational hiring practices may prolong unemployment and reduce matching efficiency.

title: Fundamental Uncertainty, Reinsurance Capacity, and the Design of a European Catastrophe Insurance Scheme

detail.title: Fundamental Uncertainty, Reinsurance Capacity, and the Design of a European Catastrophe Insurance Scheme
detail.abstract: Only about one-fifth to one-quarter of the economic losses caused by natural catastrophes in the European Union are insured, and the gap is widening as climate-related losses grow. Because uninsured losses, unlike insured ones, depress output persistently, the protection gap is a macroeconomic problem, and EIOPA and the ECB have proposed a two-pillar EU scheme combining a public-private reinsurance pool with a public disaster fund. This paper examines the proposal's central design choice: pricing the reinsurance pillar on risk-based premiums. Engaging the capital-market-imperfections literature on catastrophe insurance, it identifies the scope condition under which that literature holds, namely a knowable loss distribution, and argues that climate non-stationarity removes it. Catastrophe pricing is then better understood as conventional valuation under fundamental uncertainty, which renders private reinsurance capacity endogenously cyclical; a compact system of difference equations states the mechanism, and the 2022-2026 cycle bears it out, with prices softening rapidly while structural rationing persists. The protection gap is structural, not frictional, and risk-based premiums at EU level would reproduce it. From the French and Spanish schemes the paper derives design principles (solidarity pricing, a public tail guarantee, countercyclical funding) that connect the proposal to wider debates on the EU's fiscal architecture.

title: Caste Cannot Cure Caste: Toward a Generational Exit Framework for India's Reservation System

detail.title: Caste Cannot Cure Caste: Toward a Generational Exit Framework for India's Reservation System
detail.abstract: India's reservation system, conceived as a temporary corrective measure at the time of constitutional drafting, has now persisted for over seventy-five years without any structural review or sunset mechanism. The original constitutional intent, as articulated through Articles 15, 16, and 340, was to address historical social and educational backwardness through temporary state intervention, not to institutionalise caste as a permanent administrative category. This paper argues that the present system has produced a structural paradox: the very instrument designed to abolish caste consciousness has made caste more administratively meaningful with each passing generation. Drawing on constitutional jurisprudence, sociological literature on caste as a social construct, the developmental model of Kerala, and comparative policy analysis, this paper proposes a Generational Exit Framework that combines automatic beneficiary exclusion after upliftment, a dual-category reservation architecture separating caste-based and economic reservations, progressive de-documentation of caste identity, and strict penal enforcement of anti-discrimination law as a replacement mechanism. The argument is not that reservation must end immediately, but that reservation must be designed to end itself.

title: A Recursive Institutional Architecture for Structuring National Innovation-Policy Problems: Introducing RIPSA

detail.title: A Recursive Institutional Architecture for Structuring National Innovation-Policy Problems: Introducing RIPSA
detail.abstract: Purpose-This paper develops a Recursive Institutional Problem-Structuring Architecture (RIPSA) for national innovation systems (NIS), addressing the gap between macro-institutional diagnosis and inquiry into contested, multi-actor innovation problems. Design/methodology/approach-The paper uses a structured, non-exhaustive theory synthesis that integrates NIS, transformative innovation policy, Soft Systems Methodology (SSM), problem-structuring methods, cognitive mapping and critical systems practice. It differentiates the analytical function of each tradition and specifies rules for cross-domain translation, feedback and provisional closure. Because the paper synthesises theory rather than reports an empirical study, it follows the recognised structure for conceptual articles (Jaakkola, 2020) rather than the IMRaD template used for empirical research. Findings-Innovation challenges are conceptualised as institutionally embedded problem situations in which structures, interpretations and intervention possibilities shape one another. RIPSA links institutional diagnosis, interpretive problematisation and focused issue structuring. Its recursive mechanisms can reclassify an initially assumed innovation-system failure. Research limitations/implications-RIPSA is conceptual and requires comparative and longitudinal testing. Future studies should assess boundary adequacy, interpretive plurality, causal transparency, institutional feasibility and recursive revision. Practical implications-The architecture helps policymakers avoid premature instrument selection and develop interventions that are institutionally grounded, culturally workable and open to revision. Originality/value-The contribution is not a simple combination of NIS, SSM and cognitive mapping. RIPSA theorises how downstream inquiry can revise upstream system boundaries and failure classifications, treating recursive problem structuring as a governance capability in its own right.

title: Scope Conditions for the Market Suffocation Hypothesis: A Gated Classification Protocol

detail.title: Scope Conditions for the Market Suffocation Hypothesis: A Gated Classification Protocol
detail.abstract:
The Market Suffocation Hypothesis (MSH) holds that systemic quality upgrading follows the contraction of commercially viable outlets for low-quality or non-compliant output — quality sinks — until compliance becomes a condition of market participation. Earlier papers established the hypothesis and demonstrated it across several commodity markets, but tested it only against confirming cases, leaving its domain unspecified. This paper’s primary contribution is to specify the theory’s explanatory domain — the conditions under which the hypothesis is entitled to explain a case at all — through a falsifiable staged classification protocol applied before the hypothesis itself. Its foundation is Condition 0, a domain-defining gate requiring that the contracting channel be a genuine low-quality sink rather than a distinct product or end-use; the measurement apparatus is a supporting contribution.

Two ordered discriminators then classify admitted cases. Test 1 (Direction) separates sink closure (push) from demand-led migration (pull) by a separability criterion — a cost the closure imposes on the low-quality channel independently of any premium. Test 2 (Capture) locates the scarcity rent: it decomposes the premium on the migrating volume into the return to upgrading, cost recovery, and a residual, and asks whether an intermediary node tolls that residual above its cost of service. The Suffocation Index is reinterpreted as a measure of a closure’s completeness, not its type, and applies only after admissibility is settled. Durability is a separate persistence stage. Failure is stage-indexed: no object, wrong type, insufficient degree, or lost durability.

The central demonstration is negative. California Proposition 12, the EUDR, carbon and refrigerant closures, and correspondent-banking de-risking are admissible applications. Semiconductor capacity shifting to high-bandwidth memory, soybean oil diverted to renewable diesel, and stablecoin displacement of correspondent banking show every downstream signature of the mechanism yet fail at Condition 0, because each is substitution between distinct products or end-uses rather than the closure of a low-quality sink. The framework classifies sink-closure events and their capture topology. It does not theorise durable market power, which belongs to platform economics, the resource-based view, geographical-indication economics, and competition law. By specifying where the MSH applies, and where it does not, the paper strengthens it as a testable theory rather than an interpretive lens.

title: A General Theory of Control
affiliations: Stetson University - College of Law

detail.title: A General Theory of Control
detail.abstract:
Financial economics has explained how a firm's value responds to its capital structure and its payout policy, but not to its control structure-the allocation of authority between those who own the firm and those who run it. This Article provides the missing account. It models the attenuation of owner control as a continuous variable and proves a Modigliani-Miller invariance result: in a perfect capital market, firm value is independent of how control is allocated-the Coase Theorem turned inward, an identity never before recognized. Restore the frictions and an optimum emerges: a trade-off theory of control paralleling that of capital structure. 

The payoff is doctrinal. Introducing the limited liability shield, the Article derives a necessary and sufficient condition for its social optimality, Notably, the liability cap, the very feature by which the shield is defined, cancels. What survives weighs the shield's capital-market value against its net agency costs, and the balance fails for a specifiable class of entities: firms combining concentrated control with exposure to involuntary creditors, who can neither price nor avoid the risk of nonpayment. 

Veil piercing enforces that condition ex post. The traditional factors are reassigned: domination to the benefit side, undercapitalization to the cost side, neglected corporate formalities to neither. For involuntary-creditor claims, the Article proposes an express tiered standard: the veil presumptively thin where control is unattenuated, the single-member LLC foremost; presumptively thick where control is attenuated; contestable in between. Many courts already decide this way implicitly. The doctrine should say so explicitly.

title: Overshooting the Coordinate: Where Factor Corrections Land on Characteristic Axes

detail.title: Overshooting the Coordinate: Where Factor Corrections Land on Characteristic Axes
detail.abstract: Maximum-Sharpe spanning measures how factors expand the investment opportunity set, not where they leave pricing errors along the characteristics they are built to price. I develop a characteristic-axis diagnostic that traces model alphas across the full order induced by a predetermined characteristic. In 1967-2024 CRSP data, counterpart factors move pricing-error curves downward but land differently: profitability and momentum flatten, value overshoots on average but shifts across correction regimes, and investment crosses zero with weaker evidence. Sharpe gains do not determine these destinations, and q5's value non-rejections partly reflect wider null bands. Factor-model evaluation therefore requires both spanning and coordinate-specific pricing.

title: Infodynamics of Consciousness and Empathy
affiliations: Universidad Simon Bolivar

detail.title: Infodynamics of Consciousness and Empathy
detail.abstract: Infodynamics explores how the interactions between information and energy generates useful work, offering a framework for understanding cognition. It views consciousness as an adaptive mechanism that enables an entity, biological or artificial, to construct an internal map of itself and integrate it into its environmental models (Weltanschauung). When these models incorporate the perceived internal states of others, empathy emerges. Empathy in turn allows to secure synergistic social cooperation to build robust new social structures. By focusing on the utility of information, infodynamics uncovers how consciousness and empathy serve as evolutionary tools to enhance survival odds and stabilize social structures. This approach provides an actionable methodology for detecting consciousness in living or artificial entities, that allows optimizing the design of advanced artificial intelligence, and of future educational systems. Both will drive cultural and eventually biological evolution.

reference: Osmania Journal of International Business Studies (OJIBS), Volume XX, No.2, Pp 123-130, ISSN 00973-5372
title: Role of Travel Vloggers in Tourism Development in India – A Case Analysis of Regional Language Travel Vloggers
affiliations: Government First Grade College, Santhebennuru and Government Arts (Autonomous) College, Chitradurga

detail.title: Role of Travel Vloggers in Tourism Development in India – A Case Analysis of Regional Language Travel Vloggers

publicationDetails.detailsText: Osmania Journal of International Business Studies (OJIBS), Volume XX, No.2, Pp 123-130, ISSN 00973-5372

detail.abstract: Tourism in India has undergone significant transformation with the advent of digital media, particularly through the influence of travel Vloggers. Unlike traditional marketing campaigns, travel Vloggers offer authentic, experience-driven narratives that resonate with diverse audiences and shape their travel decisions. This paper examines how regional-language travel Vloggers from Karnataka — specifically Kannada YouTube creators — contribute to tourism development, destination awareness and visitor interest. Using secondary data from creator pages and public analytics (subscribers, total views, video counts) for five Kannada travel channels (Dr Bro, Flying Passport, Backpack With Mahalakshmi, Global Kannadiga, Lohith Kannada Traveller), we evaluate relationships between audience size and reach (views). Findings show a strong positive association between subscriber base and average views per video among the sampled channels, suggesting follower size is a useful proxy for informational reach of a vlogger. Findings reveal that travel Vloggers play a critical role in diversifying tourism flows, promoting offbeat destinations, encouraging sustainable practices, and fostering inclusivity by reaching regional-language audiences. The study concludes with policy recommendations for tourism boards, local communities, and Vloggers to maximize the positive impact of vlogging on India’s tourism sector.

title: The MIRROR Model: Multi-Model Iterative Reflection, Review, Oversight, and Reconciliation A Human-Supervised Protocol for Transparent, Evidence-Grounded Knowledge Work

detail.title: The MIRROR Model: Multi-Model Iterative Reflection, Review, Oversight, and Reconciliation A Human-Supervised Protocol for Transparent, Evidence-Grounded Knowledge Work

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the originator of the MIRROR Model and has an intellectual-property interest in its future development. The author declares no other financial or non-financial conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Importance: General-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for research, writing, interpretation, and decision preparation. Yet a fluent answer from a single model may contain factual errors, omit relevant evidence, reflect prompt framing or user preference, reproduce shared blind spots, and convey unwarranted confidence. Existing methods address parts of this problem through self-refinement, multi-agent debate, role prompting, self-consistency, retrieval, and factual verification, but these components are rarely integrated into a transparent end-user workflow with explicit human accountability. Objective: To introduce the MIRROR Model, define its conceptual and operational basis, provide a reproducible implementation workflow, and specify a prospective program for evaluating reliability, efficiency, and human-factors consequences. Design: Foundational methods paper and proposed empirical-validation protocol informed by research on iterative refinement, multi-agent deliberation, role prompting, hallucination detection, evaluator bias, sycophancy, and human-AI decision support. The MIRROR Model is implemented through Stage 0 task triage followed by eight core stages. Proposed Evaluation Measures: Primary outcomes are expert-rated factual accuracy, completeness, calibration, reasoning quality, and decision usefulness. Secondary outcomes include unsupported-claim density, correction yield, false-correction rate, source-verification accuracy, inter-rater reliability, multi-model diversity, residual disagreement, factual improvement per 1,000 generated tokens, time, cost, cost-adjusted benefit, and user overreliance. Prespecified alternative workflows include single-pass prompting, same-model self-refinement, structured single-model checklists, unblinded multi-model review, retrieval-grounded single-model response, direct primary-source lookup, and the full MIRROR workflow. Conclusions and Relevance: The MIRROR Model converts an informal practice-asking distinct AI systems to generate, critique, revise, verify, and synthesize answers-into a transparent and auditable human-supervised methodology. Its contribution lies in the integration, ordering, safeguards, and documentation of established components rather than in a claim that critique, debate, role prompting, reframing, or verification are individually new. MIRROR is not a guarantee of correctness and does not replace external evidence or qualified professional judgment. Prospective, blinded, and independently replicated studies are required before superiority over alternative workflows can be claimed.

title: International Migration, Housing Demand Measurement, and Vancouver New-House Price Forecasting
affiliations: and University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: International Migration, Housing Demand Measurement, and Vancouver New-House Price Forecasting
detail.abstract: This paper constructs a reproducible measure of occupied-dwelling use associated with international migration and asks whether the measure improves forecasts of Statistics Canada’s Vancouver New Housing Price Index. We combine annual population components for 41 census metropolitan areas over 2002–2024 with national status- and tenure-specific housing-use rates. The accounting applies a nationally calibrated reconciliation of temporary-to-permanent transitions instead of treating them as new external arrivals, and expresses the resulting flow per 1,000 occupied dwellings. We conduct a release-delay-safe, current-vintage pseudo-real-time quarterly evaluation and a retrospective annual expanding-origin comparison. An exploratory extension evaluates realized-future information diagnostics, a 19-feature monthly leading layer, horizon-specific cross-CMA partial pooling, strictly historical-error forecast combinations, and a two-hidden-layer tanh neural network. On 102 common Vancouver origins, the exponential-weight combination has four-quarter MAE 2.826 versus 3.256 for the random walk, a 13.2% reduction, but the paired Newey–West comparison is imprecise (p = .224). At eight quarters its MAE is 6.146, worse than the random walk’s 5.736. Neural MAEs are 0.907, 3.392, and 6.560 at one, four, and eight quarters; none improves on both benchmark criteria. A separate reconstruction from exact Statistics Canada The Daily releases produces 585 historical-first-release retrospective forecasts. At one quarter, AR(4)-direct MAE is 0.781 percentage points versus 0.887 for the random walk on 51 origins; the candidate-minus-random-walk descriptive interval [-0.283, 0.071] crosses zero. In the annual metropolitan-area exercise, the composition-adjusted central sensitivity likewise fails its incremental-value criterion against both the pooled base and raw total population flow in every evaluation set. A secondary purpose-built-rental exercise also fails its incremental-information criterion for both rental outcomes. The evidence therefore separates accounting coherence from incremental predictive value. The results concern new-house prices and predictive association; they do not identify a causal policy effect or establish prospective forecast superiority.

title: Is Complexity Theory Right that Bigger is Riskier? Evidence from Information Technology
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, IT University of Copenhagen, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Is Complexity Theory Right that Bigger is Riskier? Evidence from Information Technology

declarations.funderStatement: The authors wish to thank the Villum Foundation (Villum grant: 39735) and the IT University of Copenhagen for financial support.

detail.abstract: A key thesis in complexity theory is that larger ventures entail higher risk. We test the thesis for information technology (IT) cost and schedule risk. We find that, contrary to common belief, project size is not a reliable predictor of risk. The common assumption that smaller projects have lower risk should be rejected based on our findings. In fact, the smallest IT projects have the largest risk. This finding is significant, because it challenges a central tenet of complexity theory, and it shows project management practitioners that small is not necessarily safe.

title: A Diagnostic Framework for AI Agent Behavior
affiliations: Saint Mary's University, Canada - Sobey School of Business, Peking University - Guanghua School of Management and Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business

detail.title: A Diagnostic Framework for AI Agent Behavior
detail.abstract: AI agents increasingly act within the same clinical, political, scientific, and social systems that behavioral scientists study. Evaluating these systems requires source-level diagnosis: the same behavioral pattern may arise from an agent's representational substrate or from the roles, objectives, interaction structures, and governance rules that shape its expression. This Perspective proposes a diagnostic framework for AI agent behavior: layer attribution. The foundational computational layer defines what behaviors are possible through architecture, memory, perception, attention, and representation. The behavioral modulation layer shapes how those capacities are expressed through identity, resources, objectives, social interaction, institutional constraints, and governance. The framework clarifies three consequences: surrogate validity is a model-task-layer relation, human-AI divergence provides diagnostic evidence, and governance requires source attribution before intervention. Treating AI agents as behavioral actors therefore requires evaluation methods that determine where behavior originates before deciding how to explain, validate, or govern it.

title: Reimagining Economic Theory in the Age of Machine Learning and Big Data
affiliations: and Guru Nanak College (GNC)

detail.title: Reimagining Economic Theory in the Age of Machine Learning and Big Data
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital technologies and the growing availability of largescale data are transforming the way economies operate and how economic questions are studied. As economies become increasingly data-driven, Machine Learning (ML) and Big Data are providing economists with new ways to understand, model, and predict economic behaviour. This chapter explores how these technologies are reshaping economic theory by complementing traditional approaches with more dynamic, predictive, and evidence-based methods. It traces the evolution of economic thought from classical and neoclassical perspectives to modern computational approaches, highlighting the need to move beyond conventional assumption-based models in an increasingly complex digital economy. The chapter also explains the roles of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Deep Learning (DL), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Large Language Models (LLMs), and examines their applications across sectors such as finance, e-commerce, healthcare, agriculture, governance, and education, with a particular focus on India's digital transformation. Rather than replacing established economic theories, these technologies strengthen them by enabling real-time analysis, more accurate forecasting, deeper behavioural insights, and better-informed policy decisions. While challenges related to data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, and ethical governance remain, the article argues

title: Behavioral Trigger Layer for Human Cyber Resilience: A Complementary Application Model to the Helix Cyber Resilience Architecture

detail.title: Behavioral Trigger Layer for Human Cyber Resilience: A Complementary Application Model to the Helix Cyber Resilience Architecture

The Helix Cyber Resilience Architecture and this complementary work are the personal scholarly work of the author.

detail.abstract: Social-engineering attacks succeed by exploiting recurrent human exposure mechanisms — urgency, authority, curiosity, social proof, and related psychological levers — that are stable across history and merely re-delivered through contemporary digital vectors. Security-awareness programs and maturity frameworks frequently address human behavior in generic terms, without a structured, reproducible layer of behavioral triggers to guide application. This paper proposes a Behavioral Trigger Layer as a complementary application component within The Helix Cyber Resilience Architecture (Porta, SSRN DOI 10.2139/ssrn.6635660). Its central proposition is that the same behavioral trigger manifests differently across formative, operational, and governance contexts, and that observing this contextual transfer offers a practical mechanism for assessing human cyber-resilience maturity. The layer organizes nine behavioral triggers and one transversal defensive capability along two dimensions: a relatively invariant psychological dimension and a time-bound cyber-threat dimension. To address the risk of an arbitrary selection, the paper introduces a Helix Behavioral Trigger Prioritization Index (HBTPI) that combines cyber-threat-intelligence frequency, reported financial impact, cross-report prevalence, psychological grounding, and threat-taxonomy coverage into a documented, updateable ranking; the prioritization is then anchored to current threat-intelligence evidence from authoritative sources. The triggers are positioned as scenario-building components for workshops, simulations, phishing and vishing exercises, tabletop activities, and questionnaires used to observe human responses across the formative, operational, and governance contexts described by Helix. A practical application model — a calibration-and-challenger design (an anonymous profiling step followed by two scored rounds) with an aggregate, group-level maturity indicator — is presented as a proposed, simulation-based proxy that is not a validated psychometric instrument. The layer does not measure maturity; it provides structured exposure mechanisms through which maturity may be observed. The paper makes explicit that the triggers are neither the framework nor, in isolation, the measurement instrument; that the trigger set is current and updateable rather than universal; and that empirical validation, following established scale-development practice, is future work. Although designed for application within the framework, the layer may be adapted to other human-centered cyber-resilience programs. The contribution is to render trigger selection reproducible, evidence-anchored, applicable, and updateable within the framework and its broader ecosystem.

title: Is More Explicit Information Better? The Paradox of Recommendation Labeling in Online Investment Communities
affiliations: Nanjing University - School of Management and Engineering, University of Florida - Warrington College of Business Administration, University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) and Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Is More Explicit Information Better? The Paradox of Recommendation Labeling in Online Investment Communities
detail.abstract: Recommendation labels, such as bullish, neutral, or bearish tags, are increasingly used in online investment communities to explicitly convey contributors' opinions. While such labels facilitate information processing, we argue that they carry an unintended consequence: by making an opinion's stance explicit and making departures from recent consensus easier to recognize, labels heighten the salience of deviations from recent consensus. Because investors tend to interpret a larger deviation as lower credibility, the explicit labels can increase investor disagreement with deviant opinions. We test this argument using a platform-wide interface redesign on Seeking Alpha, where the platform introduced color-coded categorical labels (very bullish, bullish, neutral, bearish, and very bearish) for article-level opinions. Using this natural experiment, we find that opinion deviation is largely unrelated to comment disagreement before the redesign but becomes significantly and positively associated with disagreement afterward. This effect is attenuated when articles contain more quantitative analysis and when contributors have a stronger track record of forecasting accuracy, consistent with a credibilitybased mechanism. A controlled online experiment that orthogonally manipulates label visibility and opinion deviation replicates the pattern and confirms perceived credibility as the underlying mechanism. Finally, we show that more deviant opinions are, on average, more informative about future stock returns, yet the disagreement they provoke discourages subsequent investors from relying on them. Our findings identify a design-induced paradox: interface features intended to make opinions more explicit can inadvertently suppress the adoption of informative but nonconsensual opinions.
