detail.abstract: America's AI build-out is running into three walls: electricity, cooling, and water. Data centers already use about 4 percent of U.S. electricity and could use up to 12 percent by 2028, and most new campuses are being built in water-stressed regions where evaporative cooling consumes millions of cubic meters of freshwater a year. Project POLARIS proposes building the next generation of AI campuses on cold northern coastlines, designed as integrated energy systems: small modular reactors and hydropower supply carbon-free electricity; the ocean's deep, cold water absorbs waste heat through sealed closed-loop heat exchangers, consuming no freshwater; and before reaching the ocean, that heat warms homes, greenhouses, and fish farms. Every component operates commercially today - deep-water district cooling in Toronto since 2004, fjord-cooled data centers in Norway, Arctic renewable data centers in Iceland, small modular reactors under construction in North America. The paper develops the reference architecture and thermal-electrical balances for a 500 MW campus, proposes a U.S.-Denmark-Greenland flagship demonstration aligned with the three governments' active 2026 economic discussions, and a domestic companion track under the U.S. Department of Energy's AI-infrastructure-on-federal-lands program. The recommended first step is a joint feasibility study and twelve months of oceanographic data at candidate sites. Also published as DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21366524.

title: Bend the Form, Preserve the Will: The Contract as Bamboo in Modern Cross-Border Business

detail.title: Bend the Form, Preserve the Will: The Contract as Bamboo in Modern Cross-Border Business
detail.abstract: Most contracts are engineered to survive: force majeure, severability, carefully chosen governing law, calibrated indemnities. This defensive architecture answers binary questions in a regulatory environment that no longer produces binary events. Drawing on the allegory of the oak and the bamboo, this essay argues that survival and flexion are distinct design objectives: a contract that survives remains valid while the regulatory ground moves; a contract that flexes remains operational. The argument rests on a conceptual claim, that the contract is an expression of will rather than a rulebook, and on a structural one, that in cross-border transactions the contract does not document the business but constitutes its architecture, since no shared institutional infrastructure exists to fill its gaps. Successive regulatory waves (GDPR, the AI Act, the Data Act) have exposed the cost of rigidity: instruments that remained valid yet required wholesale renegotiation. The essay proposes three design principles for adaptive contractual architecture: declaring an immovable core and flexible instrumental layers; converting regulatory change from contingency into routine through pre-agreed adaptation mechanisms; and designing for divergence between jurisdictions. Survival, it concludes, is the floor. Flexion is the competitive edge.

title: Ambiguity, Cash Management, Investment and Financing Structure
affiliations: Hunan University and Hunan University - School of Finance and Statistics

detail.title: Ambiguity, Cash Management, Investment and Financing Structure
detail.abstract: We develop a dynamic continuous-time growth-option model in which ambiguity-averse shareholders face financing constraints. The firm is initially financed with legacy debt and equity, and investment can be funded with internal liquidity, external equity, and newly issued debt. Shareholders jointly choose cash retention, payout, investment timing, and financing. We provide closed-form solutions for equity and debt values before and after investment, together with the associated corporate policies. Furthermore, we highlight the implications of ambiguity and derive the following novel results. First, we demonstrate that ambiguity aversion only leads shareholders to have risk-taking incentives and generates shareholder-debtholder agency conflicts near liquidity default. Second, we find that ambiguity aversion makes shareholders prefer the barrier strategy to the band strategy for payout policies before investment. Third, when the amount of legacy debt is low, ambiguity aversion leads shareholders to issue more new debt, decrease the internal funding for investment, and accelerate investment. In contrast, the results are reversed when the amount of legacy debt is high.

title: Identifying Daily Oil Market Shocks: Evidence from the Hormuz Crisis

detail.title: Identifying Daily Oil Market Shocks: Evidence from the Hormuz Crisis
detail.abstract: This paper develops a daily Bayesian structural VAR model of the global crude oil market that decomposes the real price of oil into three fundamental drivers: shocks to global real economic activity, shocks to oil price expectations and shocks to physical oil supply. We combine a daily signrestriction identification strategy with a posterior filtering step based on monthly physical oil market data, which sharpens the economic interpretation of the estimated daily shocks. We apply the model to provide a real-time interpretation of the main drivers behind the 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, one of the largest and most abrupt oil price shocks of recent years. Our results show that oil supply shocks account for the bulk of the initial price surge following the closure of the Strait, aggregate demand shocks become increasingly important in sustaining elevated prices over the following weeks and expectational shocks act in the direction of mitigating the oil price surge. We further validate the model against four major historical episodes-the 2003-08 oil price boom, the Global Financial Crisis, the 2014-15 oil price collapse, and the COVID-19 pandemic-showing that the daily decomposition is consistent with the prevailing narrative of these events. The framework offers policymakers a timely tool for monitoring the structural sources of oil price fluctuations as they unfold.

detail.title: Comparative Analysis of Patents on Hydrogen Technologies in Selected Latin American Countries:  Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Mexico

publicationDetails.detailsText: Max Planck Institute for Innovation & Competition Research Paper No. 26-09
publicationDetails.journalName: Max Planck Institute for Innovation & Competition Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
This study provides a comparative analysis of patent activity related to hydrogen technologies in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia and Mexico, with a focus on hydrogen production, storage and end-use applications. Based on an initial dataset of 495 patent applications, the study examines the legal status, technological scope and ownership structure of hydrogen-related patents in the selected jurisdictions. 

The findings show that patenting activity in the region is highly concentrated in foreign companies, with limited participation by local firms, universities and research institutions. While Latin America has significant potential to become a major producer of green hydrogen, the patent landscape suggests the region currently plays a more limited role in developing and owning the key technologies that will shape the hydrogen economy.

title: Salamanca and Philadelphia: A Convergent Genealogy of Popular Sovereignty and Institutional Resistance

detail.title: Salamanca and Philadelphia: A Convergent Genealogy of Popular Sovereignty and Institutional Resistance

contentType.other: Paper submitted to 10th Annual Madrid Conference on Austrian Economics

detail.abstract: The confluence of the 500th anniversary of the School of Salamanca (1526) and the 250th anniversary of the United States Declaration of Independence (1776) in 2026 provides a critical opportunity to re-evaluate the history of early modern legal and economic thought. The present article posits that the relationship between these two intellectual traditions is best understood through a model of convergent parallelism-a mediated, trans-confessional transmission rooted in a shared Western legal heritage, rather than direct, unverified attribution. The Late Scholastic political theology of Francisco de Vitoria and Francisco Suárez developed a systematic doctrine of subjective natural rights (iura), popular sovereignty, and fiduciary constraints on state coercion that structurally mirrors the core political architecture of the 1776 Declaration. Moving beyond self-contained Whig and civic-republican historiographies, this study demonstrates how Salamanca's innovations anticipated modern constitutional rights frameworks. It traces the trans-confessional migration of these scholastic taxonomies as they were secularised by Protestant natural-law jurists-most notably Hugo Grotius, Samuel von Pufendorf, and Johannes Althusius-and documents their concrete integration into the colonial British American higher education curriculum under John Witherspoon at Princeton. Finally, the article provides a metahistorical account of the subsequent Anglo-American silence regarding this lineage. Rather than a simple accidental oversight, this absence was sustained by the early republic's self-definition within an exclusively Anglo-Whig narrative of liberty, deeply conditioned by inherited Black Legend cultural biases and ongoing geopolitical rivalries with the Spanish Empire. By evaluating these structural dynamics, the article restores a marginalised, Late Scholastic root to the global genealogy of constitutional liberty.

keywords.keywords: Handwritten medicine-name recognitionHandwritten prescription recognitionDeep learningConvolutional neural networksCNN-BiLSTMAttention-based feature fusionCross-dataset generalizationPrescription digitizationMedical image analysisBanglade

detail.abstract: Handwritten medicine-name recognition remains a challenging problem in medical informatics,particularly in low-resource healthcare settings such as Bangladesh, where handwritten prescriptionsare still widely used. This study presents a comparative evaluation of deep learning architectures forisolated handwritten medicine-name recognition using a newly constructed balanced Bangladeshihandwritten medicine-name dataset developed for this study, containing 22,190 images from 317medicine classes. Seven models were evaluated under a unified training and preprocessing protocol:five CNN-based baselines, namely VGG16, VGG19, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0, along with two hybrid fusion models, CNN-BiLSTM and CNN-Attention. In the in-domain testsetting, all models achieved Top-1 accuracies above 97%, indicating strong recognition capabilityunder the training-data distribution. DenseNet121 obtained the highest Top-1 accuracy of 98.85%,while CNN-BiLSTM achieved the highest Top-5 accuracy of 99.85% and the highest Macro F1-score of 0.987. Since the in-domain performance differences among several models were small,the results are interpreted as comparative rather than statistically conclusive superiority claims. Toexamine robustness beyond the primary dataset, an additional evaluation was designed using anindependently sourced Bangladeshi prescription dataset with 25 overlapping medicine classes. Thisexternal evaluation analyzes how model performance changes when exposed to handwriting samplesfrom a different data source. Overall, this work provides a structured comparative analysis of CNN-based, feature-fusion, attention-based, and BiLSTM-based models for handwritten medicine-namerecognition.

title: Nowcasting GDP with Digital Payments: Evidence from Uganda

detail.title: Nowcasting GDP with Digital Payments: Evidence from Uganda

publicationDetails.journalName: BAFFI Centre on Economics, Finance & Regulation Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: In developing economies, output statistics arrive with long lags and omit a large informal sector, while digital payment systems record a growing share of transactions in near real time. We assess whether these records improve GDP nowcasts in Uganda, exploiting two national systems that observe complementary segments of the economy: Mobile Money, covering retail and informal transactions, and real-time gross settlement (RTGS), covering large-value formal payments. Within a pseudo-real-time design respecting each series’ publication lag, we augment a conventional macroeconomic panel with payment data across linear and machinelearning models. Payment data cut forecast errors by up to 16 percent and rank among the most informative predictors, with up to over three times the weight of a typical macroeconomic indicator. The improvement delivered by payment data is robust to macroeconomic disturbances, such as the COVID-19 contraction. Placebo tests attribute these gains to economic content, not added predictors. Already held by central banks, payment data offer a timely, low-cost input for surveillance where conventional statistics are weakest.

title: The Financial Anatomy of a Development Trap: External-liability Servicing, Commodity Dependence, and Stalled Structural Transformation in Middle-income Economies (2000-2022)
affiliations: and Universidade Estadual de Campinas (UNICAMP) - Instituto de Economia

detail.title: The Financial Anatomy of a Development Trap: External-liability Servicing, Commodity Dependence, and Stalled Structural Transformation in Middle-income Economies (2000-2022)

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Why do many middle-income economies stall in their structural transformation, deindustrialising and reprimarising before they reach high income? Explanations usually turn on productive capabilities, the exchange rate, the commercial Dutch disease, or position in global value chains. This article adds a financial dimension that cuts across them, rooted in the most neglected part of the balance of payments-the income account. Using an annual panel of thirty-seven middle-income economies for 2000-2022, and externalliability positions measured at market value from the External Wealth of Nations database, it shows that the accumulated stock of external liabilities robustly raises the outflow of primary income (profits, dividends and interest), and that this drain anchors dependence on commodity exports. A structural typology recovers a transregional "commodity-financialised" route-most of Latin America alongside resource exporters in Eurasia, the Middle East and Africa-that carries, on average, a markedly higher income drain and commodity share and a lower manufacturing share than a manufacturing-integrated or an industrialising East Asian route. A shift-share instrument based on global financial conditions offers suggestive but not decisive evidence of a causal channel within the exposed route-the least robust of our findings, and treated as such. The commodity-financialised route remitted a net US$3.8 trillion in primary income over the period, a financial counterpart to ecologically unequal exchange, and it runs external deficits that the drain more than explains-a foreign-exchange servitude. Reindustrialisation therefore requires managing the external liability position alongside exchange-rate and industrial policy.

title: Pricing Heat: A Parametric Risk-Transfer Model for MSME Production Loss in Delhi-NCR

detail.title: Pricing Heat: A Parametric Risk-Transfer Model for MSME Production Loss in Delhi-NCR

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research was conducted independently and has no financial or professional relationship with SIDBI, Swiss Re, ICICI Lombard, Mahila Housing Trust, the Self-Employed Women’s Association, or any other institution named in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper relies entirely on publicly available secondary data (India Meteorological Department records, published research literature, and public reporting) and does not involve primary data collection from human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: In 2026, India's parametric heat insurance pilots reached Delhi and Faridabad for the first time, extending automatic weather-triggered payouts to nearly 8,500 informal women workers in the National Capital Region. These pilots, along with the earlier Women's Climate Shock initiative operating across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra, compensate individual wage loss when consecutive days of extreme heat cross a defined temperature threshold. The design leaves a distinct exposure unpriced. A factory does not stop producing because one worker's wages have been protected; it stops producing when heat halts the line itself. This paper develops a parametric pricing framework for enterprise-level production loss among Delhi-NCR's micro and small manufacturers, using India Meteorological Department temperature records to model trigger frequency, and international labour-productivity elasticity estimates, tested across a sensitivity range, to approximate output loss per heat-exceedance day. A breakeven premium is derived under three candidate trigger designs and compared against the wage-loss benchmark already operating in the region. The paper does not propose a new institution. It tests whether the underwriting logic already deployed in Delhi-NCR can be extended, and at what price, to cover the enterprise rather than only the individual within it. The findings are offered as a starting point for insurers and development-finance institutions weighing how climate risk transfer might reach India's MSME sector, which employs an estimated 110 million people and remains largely uninsured against a heat exposure it already absorbs.

title: The Life Cycle of Monetary Anchors: Credibility Accumulation, Erosion, and Recasting, 1871-2007

detail.title: The Life Cycle of Monetary Anchors: Credibility Accumulation, Erosion, and Recasting, 1871-2007
detail.abstract: Why do monetary anchors live and die? This paper reframes the rules-versus-discretion debate as a question of institutional life cycles rather than institutional types. Using recomputed monthly equity returns (Shiller S&P Composite total returns, 1871–2007), I show that anchor type—mechanical versus reputation-based—does not map onto volatility level: the classical gold standard (R2, 1879–1913) and the Great Moderation (R9, 1983–2007) produced nearly identical monthly standard deviations (3.26% vs. 3.32%; difference statistically indistinguishable from zero under block bootstrap), while the interwar gold standard (R5, 1925–1933), also a mechanical anchor, produced the highest volatility in the sample (8.89%). What distinguishes regimes is instead the state of their credibility capital—a stock that is accumulated through costly commitments, eroded through support-structure decay (mechanical anchors) or moral-hazard accumulation (reputation-based anchors), and occasionally recast after collapse. Anchor type does shape the form of fragility: at nearly identical variance, the reputation-based R9 exhibits a significantly fatter tail than the mechanical R2 (excess kurtosis 2.43 vs. 0.45, block-bootstrap 95% CI for the difference [0.56, 3.45]; the 5% most extreme months account for 42.8% vs. 31.9% of total variance, CI [2.7, 19.1] points), concentrated in rescue-adjacent episodes. A data-driven structural-break analysis (Bai–Perron) detects essentially one dominant volatility episode in 137 years—October 1929 to mid-1933—and no variance break at any other institutional boundary, corroborating both the uniqueness of the interwar failure and the proposition that mechanical-anchor erosion is statistically invisible until collapse. A sixteen-country panel (JST Macrohistory Database, 1870–1939) confirms the level proposition out of sample: pegged years display 7.8 percentage points lower equity volatility (clustered t = −4.1), but the interwar interaction fully reverses the discount (+11.7 points, t = +3.4). The framework's central construct is then measured independently of equity markets: a CPI-only pilot fails and is reported as such, but two domain-correct components—gold cover ratios for the metallic era (rising from 22.8% in mid-1878 to 56% by 1912, with the 1893–96 silver-crisis dip and the 1920 squeeze visible) and survey-expectation anchoring for the reputation era (Livingston forecasts: R7 +0.17, R8 −0.86, R9 +0.23, with the 1980 de-anchoring trough at 11.9% expected inflation)—track the framework's credibility-state ordering.A pilot credibility index built solely from price-level data yields a null result, reported as such; the measurement requirements it reveals define the framework's forward agenda. Three transition episodes—the wartime fracture of 1914–1917, the exhaustion of Bretton Woods, and the Volcker recasting—illustrate an evolutionary dynamic in which crisis-born institutional variations are selected and retained as new anchoring routines. Market prices corroborate the distributional evidence: corporate-credit spreads (Baa–AAA) were systematically compressed under mature anchors—0.67 points under Bretton Woods and 0.90 points even in 2006–mid-2007, on the eve of collapse—while regime-level equity premia turn negative precisely when credibility is in transition. The framework yields an asymmetry proposition: mechanical anchors generate reform pressures when their constraints bind, while reputation-based anchors generate moral hazard when their flexibility is exploited—a pattern consistent with the subsequent 2008 crisis.

title: Tax and the Law of Market Cycles
affiliations: Vanderbilt University - Vanderbilt Law School

detail.title: Tax and the Law of Market Cycles
detail.abstract:
The signature development in financial regulation over the past two decades has been the macroprudential turn: the recognition that healthy financial conditions sow the seeds of the next crash, and that risks tolerable in one firm become systemic when many firms take them simultaneously. This Article argues that the same logic pervades the “real” economy. In oil, shipping, mining, farming, real estate, and other capital-intensive industries, boom times encourage firms to expand production, but when many firms expand at once, prices crash, firms go under, and production contracts—eventually creating scarcity that sets off the next cycle. These market cycles harm consumers, workers, and investors. In response, the Article proposes the first comprehensive countercyclical regulatory regime for industry-specific cycles. 

Tax law should be the main tool for moderating market cycles. At present, tax makes market cycles worse: depreciation incentives are procyclical. Beyond reversing that bias, the Article proposes an excise tax on investments in new production capacity made when prices and investment exceed their long-run trends, and a subsidy for investments in new capacity made when prices and investment fall below their trends. Most of the administrative machinery this regime requires is already present in the Internal Revenue Code. The uniform capitalization rules measure capacity investments, beginning-of-construction rules distinguish investments made before and after the tax is triggered, and excise-tax and quick-refund procedures move fast enough to intervene in volatile market cycles. The Article argues that this approach is better targeted to the precise causes of market cycles than alternatives like cartels, production quotas, buffer stocks, and windfall profit taxes. Over- and undercapacity are inherent to markets, but law can stabilize the extremes.

title: Spectral Risk Parity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Cornell University - Operations Research & Industrial Engineering

detail.title: Spectral Risk Parity

keywords: Portfolio Construction JEL classification codes: G0

detail.abstract: Utilizing concepts from random matrix theory (RMT), we propose a spectral approach to constructing risk parity portfolios. This portfolio tracks the principal component portfolio while explicitly penalizing the exposure to noise. The principal components and noisy components are identified using the Marˇcenko-Pastur distribution associated with the covariance (correlation) matrix. Such portfolios are robust to noise by construction. We provide empirical evidence to show the out-performance over the equal-risk-contribution (ERC) and minimum variance (MinVar) portfolios.

title: Towards a Digital Twin for Healthier Indoor Environments Using Cellular Discrete Event Specification and Genetic Algorithms
affiliations: Carleton University and Carleton University

detail.title: Towards a Digital Twin for Healthier Indoor Environments Using Cellular Discrete Event Specification and Genetic Algorithms
detail.abstract: Experts use modeling and simulation to aid decision making to improve air quality, particularly during airborne virus outbreaks, when carbon dioxide levels can indicate infection risk. This manuscript provides a novel Digital Twin framework that uses physical space properties and Internet of Things data to create carbon dioxide dispersion models of closed spaces. The framework combines simulation models with genetic algorithms to identify optimal indoor settings for healthier environments. First, the framework creates a conceptual model representing the physical space and its key properties. Next, we develop a Cellular Discrete Event Simulation model that includes space dimensions, carbon dioxide sinks and sources, impermeable structures, breathing occupants’ data, and carbon dioxide dispersion logic. We then simulate the model and validate it against real data. We integrate genetic algorithms with our simulation engine to iteratively refine the validated simulation model and converge towards a simulation scenario representing optimal indoor settings for healthier air. The resulting model can be used to modify the real physical space to enhance air quality. Our framework and the use of genetic algorithms for indoor air quality optimization are novel contributions to the field. We use two case studies to demonstrate the framework's effectiveness, showing how the framework recommendations can be applied to physical spaces while avoiding costly and unattainable experimentation.

title: Digital Work, Earnings Premiums, and the Gender Gap: Evidence from Pakistan's Labour Force Survey 2024-25
affiliations: and Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS)

detail.title: Digital Work, Earnings Premiums, and the Gender Gap: Evidence from Pakistan's Labour Force Survey 2024-25
detail.abstract: Digital labor platforms and online work are rapidly growing in Pakistan, yet rigorous empirical evidence on the effect of this growth on Wages is very scarce. This paper uses the Labor Force Survey 2024-2025 based in Pakistan, transitioned to the global 19th ICLS standards by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, to examine three related questions: whether digital work generates a wage premium over traditional employment, whether this premium differs by gender, and the characteristics of individuals to predict entry into digital work. Using Mincer's equation, OLS regression on a restricted sample of 24406 workers, this research estimates a premium for digital work while controlling for age, gender, education, and job characteristics. The findings reveal that the conditional earnings premium is a 6.97%. Heterogeneity analysis across gender shows that digital work does not bridge the gender wage gap, as women face 22.5% earning penalty in both digital and physical work. Platform analysis also shows differences in premiums for different kinds of jobs. The probit model shows that people with higher education, especially those with higher computer qualifications and living in urban areas, have a significant increase in probability of entering and participating in the digital labor market. The results confirm that online/digital work provides a 7% earning premium but fails to reduce the gender wage gap, with returns varying across different platforms.

title: Value Coverage: A Measurement Framework for Technology Investment Booms, with a Live Application to the AI Capital Build-out

detail.title: Value Coverage: A Measurement Framework for Technology Investment Booms, with a Live Application to the AI Capital Build-out

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This is an independent research purely.
declarations.funderStatement: Personal research - only personal funding

detail.abstract: Is the AI technology boom a bubble? The question is being argued almost entirely by anecdote, one side pointing to the technology potential and the other to the spending. This paper offers a way to keep appropriate accounts rather than a direct answer to the question. It proposes that any technology investment boom can be described by three quantities, each measurable from public data. The first is private coverage (Cp): the earnings the capital throws off, set against the annual cost of owning it. The second is social coverage (Cs): the value the technology creates for the wider economy, net of its harms, against the same cost. The third is financing fragility (F ): how much of the build is paid for with outside money, and where in the structure that borrowing sits. The paper defines the three, sets out two hypotheses, one for the probability of a correction and one for its cost, in a form that can be estimated, places past booms on a simple map, and reports a live, open implementation for the AI build-out. On data to mid-2026 the headline (capital-holder) readings are Cp ≈ 0.31, Cs ≈ 0.68 at a ten-year horizon and ≈ 1.13 at thirty, and F ≈ 0.72, in the speculative range; a second, ecosystem-wide coverage line reads ≈ 0.54, a wedge of ≈ 0.23 above the capital-holders. What is offered is a measurement programme with a working instrument, and a not-yet-tested theory of bubbles. Two steps would make the central claim testable: an expectations benchmark that says what coverage the market is pricing in, and a historical backtest against the price-based crash predictor of Greenwood, Shleifer and You. Both are specified. The paper is equally clear about what such measurement cannot do. It can deliver consistency rather than accuracy, and a characterized boom rather than a prophecy.

title: When do Macroeconomic Policies Work? Global Value Chains and Industrial Performance in Low-and Middle-income Countries
affiliations: and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When do Macroeconomic Policies Work? Global Value Chains and Industrial Performance in Low-and Middle-income Countries

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Does the effectiveness of macroeconomic policy for industrial performance depend on a country's structural position in global value chains (GVCs)? We propose a conditional macro-structural framework in which macroeconomic policy and value-chain position jointly determine industrial performance, and test it for low-and middle-income countries. Using a balanced panel of 23 such countries over 2005-2020, with GVC positioning measured from the OECD TiVA database and structural sophistication from product-complexity data, we adopt a two-level design. At the broad level, the manufacturing share of GDP is robustly depressed by commodity-export concentration and manufacturing import penetration, and supported by trade openness, backward GVC participation and export sophistication. At the conditional level, the industrial effectiveness of two macroeconomic levers depends on value-chain position: the exchange rate's effect declines with commodity dependence (sharply in Latin America), and investment's effect declines with domestic-value-added intensity. The commodity result holds across three measures of industrial performance-the manufacturing share, value-added growth and industrial employment. A mediation analysis shows the exchange-rate channel is contingent because, in commoditydependent economies the currency is an endogenous outcome of commodity cycles (Dutch disease). Pooled Mean Group and error-correction estimates put the speed of adjustment toward long-run equilibrium at 15-21% per year. Value-chain position thus determines industrial performance directly and governs macroeconomic-policy effectiveness conditionally. The framework connects the macroeconomics of industrial development to the structural political economy of production.

title: The Informational Value of Media Economic Concerns for Nowcasting China's CPI Inflation
affiliations: Ghent University, Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) - Applied Economics Department and Southwestern University of Finance and Economics (SWUFE)

detail.title: The Informational Value of Media Economic Concerns for Nowcasting China's CPI Inflation

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the China Scholarship Council (#202007650028).

detail.abstract: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation in China serves as a critical monthly macroeconomic indicator for economic decision makers and policymakers. This paper develops two novel weekly economic concern indices-one derived from news articles of five major newspapers and another from government social media disclosures on 32 official Sina Weibo accounts. Using a mixed-frequency data sampling (MIDAS) regression model, we generate weekly nowcasts of CPI inflation and evaluate the predictive performance of these economic concern indices over the period from January 2013 to March 2024. Our results demonstrate significant improvements in nowcasting accuracy compared to a benchmark AR(1) model. The news-based index consistently outperforms the government social media disclosure-based index across both rolling and expanding window out-of-sample evaluations. Furthermore, incorporating both indices simultaneously reveals informational complementarity, leading to further accuracy gains. Allowing for optimized weighting of individual news outlets and government Weibo accounts via a differential evolution algorithm yields additional improvement in predictive performance, with the data-driven weighted concern indices achieving the lowest out-of-sample root mean squared errors.

title: Macroeconomic Tail Risk and Financial Statement Information: Evidence from Aggregate Earnings
affiliations: Department of Economics, National Taiwan University , National Taiwan Normal University, Department of Civic Education and Leadership and University of Liverpool Management School

detail.title: Macroeconomic Tail Risk and Financial Statement Information: Evidence from Aggregate Earnings

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None
declarations.funderStatement: National Science and Technology Council, R.O.C., Taiwan. NSTC 115-2410-H-003 -175 -MY3

detail.abstract: This study investigates how aggregate earnings shocks affect U.S. macroeconomic tail risk. We identify two asymmetric effects. First, earnings shocks disproportionately impact the lower tail of the predicted output growth distribution compared to its median or upper tail. Second, this lower-tail asymmetry intensifies when categorized by sign: negative shocks provoke systematically larger responses than positive ones. This sign asymmetry aligns with accounting conservatism, where adverse economic conditions are reported more promptly. Counterfactual analyses suggest financial conditions primarily drive these responses. Overall, our findings underscore aggregate earnings as an economically significant, underexplored source of macroeconomic tail risk.

title: Too Small to See: A Real Individual-Level GLP-1 Effect on Protein Demand Is Undetectable in Aggregate Protein-Supplement Sales and Search Data

detail.title: Too Small to See: A Real Individual-Level GLP-1 Effect on Protein Demand Is Undetectable in Aggregate Protein-Supplement Sales and Search Data

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence this work.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study used only secondary, aggregate, and publicly available data and did not involve human-subjects research, so no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: A clinical and marketing literature documents that individual users of GLP-1 receptor agonists shift consumption toward protein, and industry commentary anticipates a GLP-1-driven surge in protein-supplement demand. We ask whether this individual effect is visible in aggregate retail data. Using Euromonitor sports-protein-powder volumes for seven countries (2011-2025) and a U.S. state-by-quarter panel of Medicaid GLP-1 prescriptions and protein-powder search intent, we find no detectable macro signal, and we quantify why. A dilution accounting shows that under revealed-behavior per-user estimates the GLP-1-attributable share of observed 2018-2024 U.S. category growth is around 1% in absolute value, and even the most generous stated-willingness-to-pay ceiling caps it at about 8.5% (roughly half that at the low end of that range). The conclusion is robust to broadening the outcome from sports protein powder to the full protein-supplement category. The state panel is a precise, high-resolution null, though its outcome is population search intent rather than sales. The cross-country comparison maps the resolution limit of aggregate data, which proves too coarse to bound the micro-implied effect. The results are a quantified instance of micro-to-macro disconnect: a real individual effect, scaled by a small treated share, stays below aggregate visibility.

title: The Evolution of Retail Investors: From Speculation to Fundamentals
affiliations: Queen Mary University of London

detail.title: The Evolution of Retail Investors: From Speculation to Fundamentals
detail.abstract: Using millions of Reddit stock discussions, I characterize retail investors by the types of firms they discuss. Principal component analysis reveals a dominant axis separating users drawn to volatile, lottery-like stocks from those focused on fundamentals. Investors move along this axis: discussion shifts toward fundamentals with experience, and back toward speculation after viral posts displaying large gains; losses produce no comparable response. These episodes reach the market: the day after a viral gain, retail's share of trading rises in speculative stocks and those stocks become less stable; the composition of the crowd and the stability of prices move together.

title: Exploring The Cycling-related Policies and Socioeconomic Disparities: A Comparative Study of Bradford, Manchester and Bristol, United Kingdom

detail.title: Exploring The Cycling-related Policies and Socioeconomic Disparities: A Comparative Study of Bradford, Manchester and Bristol, United Kingdom

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors report there are no competing interests to declare.

Participants were provided with an information sheet detailing the survey and data handling procedures, and consent was obtained before the survey commenced.

detail.abstract: Over the last two decades, there has been a rise in cycling-related policies and investments in the UK, yet national cycling levels are somewhat stagnant. Furthermore, existing evidence suggests that the interventions do not benefit everyone equally; whether a person cycles or not is influenced by their gender, age, income and ethnicity amongst other factors. Policy documents from Bradford, Manchester and Bristol, as well as a survey of 330 participants are analysed to explore the differences in cycling levels of the three cities and within the socioeconomic groups. This is done by reducing the dimensions of the data through factor analysis and then creating a binary logistic regression model. Perceived quality of cycling infrastructure, gender, age, and household income have a considerable impact on a person's decision to cycle, whilst the effect of ethnicity is ambiguous. There is significant unmet demand for cycling, especially from underrepresented groups who are often deterred by the inadequate cycling conditions. Childhood cycling should be highly encouraged since the habit is likely to continue into adulthood, and non-cyclists aged 55 or over are more reluctant to undertake cycling. It is expected that provision of safe, accessible, and segregated cycling infrastructure combined with short-term campaigning and support will not only increase cycling levels, but also ease the inequalities in cycling.

title: Refugee Absorption and Electoral Change: Evifence from the Indian Partition
affiliations: and University of Luxembourg

detail.title: Refugee Absorption and Electoral Change: Evifence from the Indian Partition
detail.abstract: The 1947 Partition of British India triggered the largest forced migration of the twentieth century, redistributing millions of refugees across newly independent India. We study whether this demographic shock left a lasting imprint on democratic politics. Combining district-level refugee shares from the 1951 Census with constituency-level electoral data covering Indian state assembly elections between 1960 and 2007, we estimate the long-run effects of refugee settlement on electoral competition. We find that constituencies exposed to larger refugee inflows exhibit higher voter turnout, narrower victory margins, and a lower likelihood of electing candidates from national parties. Instead, refugee settlement shifted electoral support toward regional parties and contributed to the long-run denationalization of political competition. Our findings show that large demographic shocks can leave enduring political legacies, reshaping patterns of political representation and party competition long after displacement itself has ended.

title: National Visions and Domestic Investment: Coordination without Transformation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: National Visions and Domestic Investment: Coordination without Transformation
detail.abstract: National visions-formal long-term strategic plans adopted at head-of-state level-have become nearuniversal across the developing world, yet no crosscountry evidence exists on their macroeconomic effects. Using a difference-indifferences design on 22 non-oil vision-adoption episodes across six world regions (1970-2020), I find that adoption is associated with an increase in gross fixed capital formation of 3.1 percentage points of GDP (p = 0.003), positive in 17 of 22 episodes. The effect builds over two to three years and persists for at least five. Temporal and outcome placebo tests, a Fisher permutation test (p < 0.001), oil-country falsification, and pre-treatment balance checks support a causal interpretation. Critically, foreign direct investment does not respond (p = 0.21), and GDP growth shows only a transient spike. The pattern suggests that visions function as coordination devices that mobilize domestic capital but do not attract foreign investment or generate sustained growth. National visions resolve a coordination problem (where to invest?) but not a selection problem (invest in what?).

title: Does Better Data Mean Better Finances? Statistical Capacity and Fiscal Sustainability in Africa
affiliations: University of Dschang - Faculty of Economics and Management, Nkafu Policy Institute, Nkafu Policy Institute, University of Dschang, University of Yaounde II and Nkafu Policy Institute

detail.title: Does Better Data Mean Better Finances? Statistical Capacity and Fiscal Sustainability in Africa

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict of interest
declarations.ethicsApproval: No consent
declarations.funderStatement: No funding

detail.abstract: Despite theoretical arguments linking statistical capacity to fiscal performance, no empirical study has explicitly tested whether improvements in statistical systems enhance fiscal sustainability in Africa, nor has it identified the transmission channels. This study fills that gap. Using panel data for 54 African countries from 2016 to 2023, we employed pooled OLS, Driscoll-Kraay, quantile regression, Lewbel (2012) IV, and mediation analysis to examine the effect of the World Bank's Statistical Performance Index (SPI) on fiscal sustainability. Results consistently show that higher statistical capacity significantly improves fiscal sustainability: a one-point increase in SPI raises the primary-balance-based sustainability measure by 0.19-0.21 units. The effect is robust to alternative measures, disaggregated SPI components, outlier exclusion, and regional truncation. Quantile regressions reveal larger marginal returns for countries already in the upper tail of fiscal performance. Mediation analysis indicates that governance quality, particularly regulatory quality, corruption control, and the rule of law, accounts for 25-63% of the total effect. Policy implications include prioritising statistical investment in fiscal infrastructure, targeting governance channels, differentiating investments by capacity level, leveraging specific SPI subcomponents, and incorporating statistical capacity into debt sustainability frameworks. These findings establish statistical capacity as an actionable lever for fiscal resilience in Africa.

title: Memories of the Stock Market
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)

detail.title: Memories of the Stock Market
detail.abstract: Factors such as personality or sentiment can color both recall and expectations across individuals and thus induce spurious associations between the two. Fortunately, it is a hallmark of (faulty) memory that a refresher can correct it. This makes it possible to isolate the causal within-subject link. In a survey here, respondents were asked to recall the 2025 and 2020-2025 S&P 500 market rates of return. They were also asked for expected rates of return before and after they were shown the correct historical values. The results provide strong evidence that memory plays a central role. Furthermore, memory correction worked not only through changing recall and expected returns, but also through changing "typical return" assessments.

title: Situational Fatherhood Archetypes: A Practice Framework for Community-Based Engagement Grounding a CHW Engagement Framework in Fatherhood Research, Trauma-Informed Care, and Behavior Change Science
affiliations: Independent

The paper presents a practice framework developed from professional experience and grounded in a synthesis of existing research and theory.
