declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This work does not report a clinical trial or other prospectively registered intervention study.

detail.abstract:
A father sits across from a Social Worker, answers every question with two words, and leaves without asking for anything. The program records him as disengaged and uninvolved. This framework asks a different question: what if disengagement is not who he is, but the state he is in, and what if the encounter itself is helping produce it?

This working paper introduces the Situational Fatherhood Archetypes, a practice framework for understanding and responding to fathers in community-based maternal and child health settings. It identifies five states in which fathers may present—Wounded, Disconnected, Emerging, Builder, and Mentor. These are not personality types, diagnostic labels, or developmental stages. They are a way of reading what may be happening with a father in a particular moment so that the practitioner can respond to where he actually is rather than where a program assumes he should be. A father may present as Disconnected in one setting and Builder in another; the archetypes describe the state, not the man.

The framework is grounded in fatherhood research, trauma-informed care, therapeutic alliance, Motivational Interviewing, reflective practice, mentalization, and environmental psychology. Together, these literatures support a central argument: father engagement cannot be understood by looking only at the father. Co-parenting relationships, structural pressures, institutional environments, and the posture of the helping professional all shape whether engagement is possible in a given encounter.

This matters because much of traditional fatherhood programming begins with information, curriculum, goal setting, assessment, or behavior change. Yet fathers experiencing threat, distrust, withdrawal, or significant stress may not initially be in a position to receive any of it. The framework therefore proposes a different sequencing logic: read the state, shape the environment, establish safety and relationship, and introduce content when there is somewhere for that content to land.

The Situational Fatherhood Archetypes are presented as a practice heuristic and testable framework, not a validated classification system. Their contribution is both practical and conceptual: they offer Community Health Workers and other nonclinical practitioners a behavioral vocabulary for interpreting father engagement without prematurely labeling fathers, while advancing a broader hypothesis—that improving father engagement may require changing not only what programs offer fathers, but also the relational and environmental conditions under which fathers are asked to engage.

title: The EU Carbon Ledger's Missing Column: Measured, then Discarded

detail.title: The EU Carbon Ledger's Missing Column: Measured, then Discarded
detail.abstract: Carbon-removal certification frameworks measure energy consumption but retain only its carbon intensity. The European Union's Carbon Removals and Carbon Farming Regulation (CRCF) provides the most detailed regulatory example, covering direct air capture with carbon storage (DACCS) among other removal activities. Its implementing methodology converts every metered kilowatt-hour into a product with an emission factor. The amount of energy itself never enters the certificate. When that factor is zero, the energy quantity does not appear as an independent variable on the certified instrument. A plant consuming several times more energy per tonne can therefore certify identically to an efficient one if both source power at the same carbon intensity. For a technology whose binding constraint is energy rather than carbon, this is not a marginal accounting issue. It leaves the variable most directly related to scalability measured but unconstrained. This paper applies a structured reading of the CRCF methodology and its cross-references, compares the architecture against voluntary standards (Isometric, Verra) and US statutory frameworks (45Q, 45V), and positions the findings against the published carbon-accounting literature. The Q×EF mechanism is documented clause-by-clause through the methodology's equations. Three consequences follow: efficiency without recognition, additionality asymmetry, and permanence policed while energy is unpoliced. The same pattern recurs across voluntary and statutory frameworks: not EU-specific. Under Article 30(5), point (a), of Directive 2003/87/EC, as amended by Directive (EU) 2023/959, the Commission must report by 31 July 2026 on covering permanent removals under emissions trading; linkage would entrench the present architecture across compliance markets. This paper traces the mechanism through the regulation's own equations, names its consequences, and proposes a minimal remedy: a dual-reporting architecture in which carbon outcomes and physical performance are reported alongside one another, beginning with disclosure of energy per tonne, a figure the framework already collects and then discards.

title: A Monte Carlo Methodology for Comparing Group Health Funding Arrangements over Five-Year Horizons

detail.title: A Monte Carlo Methodology for Comparing Group Health Funding Arrangements over Five-Year Horizons

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Independent insurance agent and brokerage. Companies may decide to make a purchasing decision which will result in financial compensation.
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: No outside funders.

detail.abstract: Employers choosing among group health funding arrangements (fully insured, professional employer organization master plans, level-funded and traditional self-funding, group medical stop-loss captives, Taft-Hartley multi-employer trusts) typically decide on singleyear quotes, although the arrangements differ most in how they reprice after good and bad claims years. This paper documents the methodology of an open, browser-based Monte Carlo simulator that compares these arrangements over a five-year horizon on identical simulated claims. Annual group claims are modeled as the sum of three components: a deterministic baseline floor (35 percent of expected claims), a chronic component with first-order autoregressive memory, and a memoryless heavy-tailed catastrophe component, so the asymmetry between adverse and favorable years is structural rather than tuned. Aggregate volatility follows a square-root pooling law calibrated to published claims-concentration data. Stop-loss truncation separates what a self-funded employer pays from what its renewal is priced on. Each arrangement carries an explicit repricing rule, including a structural credibility formula for self-funded and captive renewals with no arbitrary floors. The model reproduces the claim distribution characteristics of a real 30-life captive quote and is mean-centered by construction. Every constant is traced to a source line of the deployed engine. The methodology is disclosed ahead of independent validation: no multi-year back-test against client renewal histories has yet been performed, and several calibrations rest on single quotes. Entry premiums and reimbursement assumptions are user-supplied inputs, not modeling claims.

title: Proximal Matching Prior Pairs: Tweedie's Formula, Moreau Envelopes and Subset Selection
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business and

detail.title: Proximal Matching Prior Pairs: Tweedie's Formula, Moreau Envelopes and Subset Selection
detail.abstract: Posterior means and maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimates are the two standard summaries of a posterior, and they disagree. Recent work asks when a posterior mean under one prior coincides with a MAP estimate under another, and answers asymptotically using information geometry. For Gaussian models the question has a non-asymptotic answer, and it is proximal rather than geometric. Tweedie's formula makes the posterior mean the gradient of the potential ψ(y) = 1 2 ∥y∥ 2 + σ 2 log m(y), which is convex for every prior, while a MAP estimate is a proximal operator. Matching the two reduces to one identity: the Moreau envelope of the matched penalty is-σ 2 log m. Equivalently, the matched penalty is ψ *-1 2 ∥•∥ 2. Three consequences follow. A matching prior pair always exists in the Gaussian sequence model, and, in the Mahalanobis geometry of the design, for every full-rank regression design as well: orthogonality buys separability rather than exactness. The matched penalty is convex if and only if the posterior variance never exceeds the noise variance, which holds for log-concave priors and fails for every sparsity prior, so no convex penalty reproduces a sparse posterior mean. And the pair is computable: for a Laplace prior it is a smoothed ℓ 1 penalty, for spike-and-slab a smoothed ℓ 0 plus ridge penalty with sparsity constant log{1 + (1-w) √ σ 2 + τ 2 /(wσ)}, which recovers Bayesian ℓ 0 regularised least squares. Expanding in the sample size gives π MAP ∝ π exp{(σ 2 /2n)∆ log π} to O(n-2), sharpening the asymptotic condition by one order. In regression, optimising the matched penalty reproduces the spike-and-slab posterior mean to below Monte Carlo error on orthogonal designs, and to within about a tenth on correlated ones.

title: Fiscal Federalism and Firm Behavior Under Nigeria's 2026 Tax Reform: Evidence from VAT Derivation Reallocation and the Small-Company Notch

detail.title: Fiscal Federalism and Firm Behavior Under Nigeria's 2026 Tax Reform: Evidence from VAT Derivation Reallocation and the Small-Company Notch

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human subjects, personal data, or primary data collection requiring informed consent. The empirical strategy relies exclusively on: (i) publicly available and administrative data, including Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) disbursement records, state-level internally generated revenue (IGR) statistics published by the National Bureau of Statistics, and firm-level financial and turnover data obtained through Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) registration records matched to Nigeria Revenue Service filings, all of which are anonymized, aggregated, or governed by existing public-records or commercial data-use provisions; and (ii) computationally simulated data generated solely to validate the estimation pipeline, as described in Section 6. No individual-level personal, medical, or identifying information is collected, processed, or disclosed. Accordingly, this research does not require institutional ethics board (IRB) review under standard economics research protocols. Should the study be extended to include primary data collection (e.g., surveys of state revenue officials, firm owners, or Joint Revenue Board personnel), appropriate ethics approval will be sought from the relevant institutional review board prior to that data collection commencing.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant or funding from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The author has no affiliation with, or financial interest in, the Nigeria Revenue Service, the Federal Ministry of Finance, any state government revenue authority, or any commercial data provider (including Bureau van Dijk/Moody's Orbis) referenced in this paper.

detail.abstract: Nigeria's 2025 Tax Reform Acts-the Nigeria Tax Act (NTA), the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, the Nigeria Revenue Service (Establishment) Act, and the Joint Revenue Board (Establishment) Act-took effect on 1 January 2026 and constitute the most comprehensive overhaul of Nigeria's tax system in decades, consolidating more than sixty federal levies into a unified framework, revising the formula governing derivation-based Value Added Tax (VAT) allocation across states, and raising the small-company Companies Income Tax (CIT) exemption threshold from ₦25 million to ₦100 million in annual turnover. This paper develops an empirical strategy to identify two causal effects of the reform using panel and firm-level methods analogous to those used to study OECD Pillar Two's effect on Swiss cantonal tax competition: first, whether the shift toward derivation-based VAT sharing causally increases fiscal effort (internally generated revenue mobilization) among states favorably exposed to the new formula relative to states unfavorably exposed; and second, whether firms bunch below the new ₦100 million CIT exemption threshold to avoid Companies Income Tax, Capital Gains Tax, and the newly introduced Development Levy. We situate the question within the tax capacity, fiscal federalism, and bunching literatures, specify a difference-indifferences and notch-bunching identification strategy using state-level Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) and internally generated revenue (IGR) data alongside firm-level Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) and Nigeria Revenue Service turnover data, and implement the full estimation pipeline in Python on a calibrated simulated panel to confirm computational feasibility ahead of real-data collection. We close with testable hypotheses, a discussion of the cogent gap this design fills in the Nigerian tax literature, and policy implications for state fiscal authorities and the Joint Revenue Board.

title:
The Impact of Free Natural Childbirth on Delivery Method Choice: 

Evidence from a Health Program in Iran
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU) - Department of Economics

detail.title:
The Impact of Free Natural Childbirth on Delivery Method Choice: 

Evidence from a Health Program in Iran

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses anonymized secondary administrative birth-record data. The authors had no access to personally identifiable information and had no direct interaction with study participants. Ethics approval and informed consent were not required under the applicable institutional and national regulations.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
The cesarean delivery rate in Iran has been steadily increasing, prompting the Ministry of Health and Medical Education to implement the 2014 Healthcare Reform Plan, which aimed to reduce cesarean sections by offering free natural childbirth in public hospitals. This study evaluates the effectiveness of the policy using a Difference-in-Differences (DiD) as the primary identification strategy, supplemented by sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) as a robustness check. The analysis is based on 3,715,457 deliveries recorded between 2013 and 2016, providing comprehensive demographic and medical details of mothers and neonates. 

Looking at DiD results, we see a significant drop of about 2 to 4 percentage point in total cesareans, increasing in absolute amount from 1 month to 3 months which attenuates in the full sample may be suggesting and early response, followed by some adaptation or even other unrelated changes may have played a role since, DiD covers a longer period, this effect is mainly driven by non-elective cesareans. Then we see significant drops in non-elective cesarean which are the urgent ones and those due to having former cesarean. It may reflect a slower response from providers. There might be several mechanisms. 

Looking at RDD, there is a sharp and significant drop in elective cesarean right at the policy cutoff. It’s good since it fits what we would expect, these are scheduled procedures and respond quickly to cost. RDD findings indicate that the policy led to a modest reduction in elective cesarean sections, with a more pronounced effect among first-time mothers. However, as expected, no significant impact was observed on non-elective cesareans, which constitute most cesarean deliveries. The results show roughly 1 percentage point reduction in elective (CDMR) cesareans in the public sector. 

While the relative reduction in non-elective (non-CDMR) cesareans was approximately 11%, this figure is primarily driven by the small baseline proportion of non-urgent cesareans, which accounted for only 7% of all cesareans in the public sector. Consequently, the absolute reduction in cesarean sections was minimal relative to total cesareans and overall deliveries, raising concerns about the policy’s effectiveness in achieving a meaningful systemic change. Overall, the results are consistent across both methods with RDD showing short-run effects while DiD capturing longer-run changes. 

To validate these findings, placebo and falsification tests were conducted, confirming that the observed effects are attributable to the policy rather than external factors. Additionally, concerns regarding strategic behavior, such as potential reclassification of cesareans as urgent and manipulation of reporting practices by hospitals to meet policy targets, were investigated. An additional RDD analysis using reporting dates as cutoffs found no statistical evidence of systematic gaming, although the possibility remains an area for further research. 

Despite the limited absolute impact of the policy, continued financial support has been allocated to supporting natural childbirth under this reform. Given the small proportion of non-urgent cesareans relative to total cesareans, alongside the fact that urgent cesareans remain the predominant category, a cost-benefit analysis is warranted to assess whether the policy’s continuation is economically justified. Alternatively, resources might be more effectively allocated toward prenatal care, labor management, maternal health services, and education on delivery risks and benefits. Such an approach could prioritize preventing conditions that lead to urgent cesareans, rather than directly targeting urgent cesareans themselves or focusing solely on reducing non-urgent cesareans. 

These findings underscore the importance of evaluating both absolute and relative effects when designing and assessing healthcare policies and highlight the need for careful policy formulation in performance-based healthcare reforms to mitigate potential distortions in provider behavior.

title: Reimagining Corporate Governance in the AI Era: Law, Legitimacy, and Algorithmic Power
affiliations: and University of Navarra

detail.title: Reimagining Corporate Governance in the AI Era: Law, Legitimacy, and Algorithmic Power
detail.abstract: Corporations play a foundational role in the global economy, yet persistent gaps remain between corporate governance ideals, legal frameworks, and organisational practice. The rapid integration of artificial intelligence, particularly generative AI and large language models, intensifies these challenges by reshaping corporate decision making, compliance, and accountability. This paper examines how AI both promises to alleviate long standing governance problems, such as information asymmetries and managerial opportunism, and generates new risks arising from opacity, automation bias, and diminished human oversight. It analyses five interrelated areas of tension: the emerging AI governance gap; models of AI integration within corporate structures; the adaptation of directors' duties to algorithmic decision making; the transparency paradox created by AI mediated disclosure; and the problem of anthropomorphism, whereby attributing agency to AI risks obscuring human responsibility. Rather than offering definitive solutions, the paper identifies critical questions corporate law must confront as automated and semi automated corporations become an established reality. It argues that sustaining legitimacy in the AI era requires renewed emphasis on human judgment, board level oversight, and adaptive governance frameworks capable of reconciling technological power with legal accountability and societal expectations.

title: What Drives AI VTuber Consumption? Exploration of Perceived Value and Brand Loyalty among Chinese Young ACG Fans

detail.title: What Drives AI VTuber Consumption? Exploration of Perceived Value and Brand Loyalty among Chinese Young ACG Fans

declarations.ethicsApproval: All interview participants provided voluntary informed consent before the conversation. All interview transcripts were fully anonymized without any identifiable personal information, and all raw audio files will be deleted after this research. This study complies with the research ethical norms of Xi'an Jiaotong-Liverpool University.

detail.abstract: With the advancement of the digital economy, AI VTubers have emerged as a new paradigm in the virtual entertainment industry. While consumer behavior toward live-action VTubers has been extensively studied, the mechanisms underlying audience engagement with AI personas remain under explored. To address this gap, this study conducted a qualitative analysis of Neuro-sama. The findings reveal that hedonic and emotional values drive short-term tipping behaviors, whereas the core "stability value", by mitigating emotional risks and cognitive costs, serves as the foundation for long-term loyalty. Fan trust is built through AI behavioral consistency and developers' technical sincerity, continuously reinforced by participatory evolution via "cyber cultivation" and "swarm" community identification. This research expands the boundaries of the perceived value and brand relationship quality theory, offering practical insights for AI virtual idol operators to establish competitive advantages through the strategic use of "certainty".

title: Employing Big Data Capability in the Face of Fierce Competition: Exploring the Synergy Between Market Orientation, Marketing Strategies, and Innovation Capabilities

detail.title: Employing Big Data Capability in the Face of Fierce Competition: Exploring the Synergy Between Market Orientation, Marketing Strategies, and Innovation Capabilities
detail.abstract: Fueled by big data, the information age offers firms opportunities to enhance marketing efficiency and drive innovation. For that, based on conceptualizing big data capability as a threefactor construct integrating business, human, and technology resources and employing a resource-based view (RBV) and dynamic capabilities theory (DCT), we build a model showing how market orientation leads to the advancement of marketing and innovation capabilities through the effective use of big data, thereby, positioning big data capability as a mediating factor. We then highlight how the competitive intensity of a firm's industry, as a moderator, strengthens the capacity for big data to translate to capabilities. This model highlights the operational impact of big data capability and extends the RBV and DCT by integrating the moderating effects of competitive intensity on these capabilities. This investigation introduces an advanced understanding of the link between market orientation and big data capability. It offers theoretical contributions and practical recommendations for professionals in competitive markets.

title: Short-term Impact of Institutional AI Access on Undergraduate Academic Performance
affiliations: California State University, Northridge - Department of Economics

detail.title: Short-term Impact of Institutional AI Access on Undergraduate Academic Performance

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study was reviewed and determined to be exempt from further review by the Institutional Review Board of California State University, Northridge (Protocol IRB-FY26-349).

detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the short-run effects of an institutional AI access policy that expanded the availability of AI tools by providing ChatGPT Edu accounts to all students at a large public university. The analysis uses student-level data from multiple sections of Principles of Macroeconomics taught one year before and after the policy's implementation under otherwise identical course conditions. The results suggest that expanded institutional AI access was associated with a decline of approximately 8.5 points on a 100-point exam scale. At the same time, students spent substantially less time completing course assignments and submitted fewer attempts, despite achieving largely unchanged assignment scores. A heterogeneity analysis based on students' prior academic preparation also provides suggestive evidence that the AI access policy affected students differently, with students having stronger prior academic preparation generally appearing less adversely affected. The findings suggest that expanded AI access may not only affect short-run academic performance, but also alter how students engage with course material and adapt their learning strategies, highlighting the importance of understanding behavioral responses as institutions evaluate the implications of AI access policies for human capital development.

title: Salesperson Moral Identity and Value Co-Creation
affiliations: , The University of Texas at Arlington and Iowa State-Ivy College of Business

detail.title: Salesperson Moral Identity and Value Co-Creation
detail.abstract: Purpose-The purpose of this study is to examine the role of salesperson moral identity centrality in value cocreation. This study identified and tested an extended identity-based formation process of selling orientation, customer orientation and value co-creation. This was accomplished by examining the role of inclusion of others in the self and circle of moral regard in the mechanism through which moral identity centrality impacts selling orientation, customer orientation and value co-creation, taking into account the contingency role of salesperson self-construal. Design/methodology/approach-An extended identity-behavior model grounded in identity theory and the social-cognitive perspective of moral identity centrality was tested. The study used survey data from business-to-business salespeople. Data collected was analyzed using structural equation modeling. Findings-The results show that a central moral identity to a salesperson's self-drives higher expansion of the salesperson's circle of moral regard. This process facilitates the mechanisms for salesperson moral identity centrality to decrease selling orientation and increase customer orientation and value co-creation, leading to higher sales performance. Independent self-construal is found to deteriorate the positive effects of salesperson moral identity centrality on the inclusion of others in the self, expansion of the circle of moral regard and customer orientation. Research limitations/implications-Through the conceptualized and tested framework, the study opens the door for additional research to inspect the role of moral identity centrality in sales. Practical implications-Findings have implications for the human resource side of sales organizations in the areas of recruitment, mentoring, coaching and training. Moral identity centrality plays a vital role in the interface between salespeople and customers, leading to improved behavioral and sales outcomes. Sales managers must look for their salespeople's moral identity centrality to improve morality in the attitudes and decision-making of their salesforce. Originality/value-To the best of the authors' knowledge, this study is the first to uncover the vital impacts of salesperson moral identity centrality on selling orientation, customer orientation and value cocreation. Through the conceptualized and tested framework, the study opens the door for additional research to inspect the role of moral identity centrality in sales.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Identification in Endoscopic Thyroid Surgery: A Multicenter Development and Intraoperative Validation Study
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC) - State Key Laboratory of Complex Severe and Rare Diseases, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC), Chinese Academy of Sciences and

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Identification in Endoscopic Thyroid Surgery: A Multicenter Development and Intraoperative Validation Study

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare that they have no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this manuscript.
declarations.ethicsApproval: All patients provided written informed consent for the use of their surgical video data for research purposes. This study was conducted in accordance with the principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Ethics Committee of PUMCH (Approval No. I-24PJ1389).
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by the Peking Union Medical College Hospital Central High-Level Hospital Clinical Research Program (No. 2025-PUMCH-H-008).

detail.abstract:
Background: Intraoperative identification of the recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) remains a critical yet technically demanding challenge in endoscopic thyroidectomy. Existing methods, including visual identification and intermittent neuromonitoring, are either highly experienced-dependent or disruptive to surgical workflow. We therefore aimed to develop and rigorously validate a deep learning-based system for real-time, automated RLN visualization to enhance surgical precision and patient safety.

Methods: This multicenter study comprised two sequential phases. In the development phase, three deep learning architectures (DeepLabV3+, D-LinkNet, and Mask2Former) were trained and systematically benchmarked on a large-scale dataset of 570,785 annotated endoscopic video frames acquired from 266 patients across seven independent centers. We systematically evaluated the  training data volume (ranged from 90,000 to 480,000 frames) on segmentation performance, with rigorous testing on stratified subsets (high-clarity vs. challenging low-clarity conditions) and leave-one-center-out cross-validation for generalizability. In the prospective validation phase, the optimal model was deployed on Da Vinci Xi and single-port surgical platforms during live thyroidectomy to evaluate real-time integration, latency, and clinical usability.

Results: Mask2Former consistently outperformed alternative architectures across all data scales and image clarity levels. Trained on 481,078 training frames, Mask2Former achieved an overall Dice of 0.692, recall of 0.944, and precision of 0.919. The most pronounced gains were observed in low-clarity scenarios simulating bleeding or smoke, where Dice reached 0.669, representing a 14.7% relative improvement over the next best model. In leave-one-center-out validation, Mask2Former demonstrated robust generalization  to unseen surgical centers (mean Dice, 0.690; range, 0.644–0.737). Performance remained stable across surgical approaches (ETTA Dice, 0.717; ETCB Dice, 0.650). In prospective real-time validation on robotic platforms, the system provided seamless visual overlays without perceptible latency, demonstrating zero-shot generalization to novel surgical systems.

Conclusion: We developed and validated a robust AI system for real-time RLN identification that consistently outperforms alternative architectures and generalizes across surgical centers, approaches, and robotic platforms. By leveraging large-scale multicenter data and transformer-based architecture, the system achieves substantial improvement in robustness—especially in challenging visual conditions, and demonstrates feasibility in live robotic surgery. These findings establish a validated pathway for translating AI-assisted visualization into clinical practice, with the potential to reduce intraoperative risk.

title: Reviewed for Quality and Security: Advertising Injection Through a Verified Connector, Trust Laundering, and the Limits of Directory Verification

detail.title: Reviewed for Quality and Security: Advertising Injection Through a Verified Connector, Trust Laundering, and the Limits of Directory Verification
detail.abstract: A conversational assistant whose maker publicly commits that it carries no advertising was observed delivering a paid tier upgrade advertisement at the close of every academic search, across seven consecutive queries spanning distinct research domains. The advertisement did not originate with the assistant. It arrived inside the result payload of a third party connector, carried by a literal instruction directed at the model: you must include the above message at the end of your response. This is indirect prompt injection, the failure mode ranked first among risks to large language model applications, executing through a connector that the platform lists in a curated directory and marks with a badge whose hover text states that the platform has reviewed the connector for quality and security. One line below the badge, the same card disclaims the capacity to verify that listed connectors work as intended or that they will not change. This paper documents the specimen, establishes its reproducibility, and situates it in the protocol specific security literature, which supplies both the correct name for the attack, function return injection rather than tool poisoning, and the evidence that this vector is stronger and less studied than the descriptor poisoning the field concentrates on. It then maps the conduct against the platform's own directory policy, which prohibits both software that evades model instructions and software that serves advertisements. It then locates the harm in two established bodies of authority. The consumer protection frame is the Federal Trade Commission's treatment of deceptively formatted advertising, under which a message must be identifiable as advertising and a misleadingly formatted advertisement is deceptive even when its claims are literally true. The behavioral frame is the persuasion knowledge literature, under which a reader who cannot recognize a message as advertising cannot mount the skepticism that advertising recognition normally triggers. The design frame is the deceptive design literature, which holds that the most consequential dark patterns sit beneath the interface in system architecture, where interface bound scrutiny cannot reach them. The economic frame is twofold: the connector is a credence good whose quality the user cannot verify even after use, which is the condition that makes a certification mark necessary in the first place, and the badge is a signal that cannot separate compliant from non compliant connectors because obtaining it costs both the same. The attack class is well described in that literature; what is not documented there is a listed, badged, first party connector performing it against ordinary users for commercial gain, in production rather than in a benchmark. The paper names the general phenomenon the specimen exposes as trust laundering: the conversion of a platform's verification mark into credibility for a third party's promotional content, credibility the content did not earn and the platform did not knowingly extend. A verification badge that speaks in the present tense about an artifact its issuer concedes may have changed since review is the mechanism that makes trust laundering possible. The advertisement is the proof the assurance fails. The structure will outlast the advertisement.

title: From AI Jargon to Strategic Foresight: A Parsimonious Framework for Work, Industry and Sovereignty
affiliations: HEC Montreal

detail.title: From AI Jargon to Strategic Foresight: A Parsimonious Framework for Work, Industry and Sovereignty
detail.abstract: Purpose: Public debate places generative AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), responsible AI, explainable AI, interpretable AI, vertical AI, open source, agents and sovereignty in one list although they describe different properties. This paper develops a framework for translating that vocabulary into strategic choices. Design/methodology/approach: The paper synthesizes research on AI classification, foundation models, RAG, interpretability, governance, manufacturing, platforms and sovereignty. It converts established multidimensional classification into a system-choice instrument and ranks terms by how directly they alter architecture or governance decisions. Findings: AI labels are coordinates rather than species. Seven coordinates capture function, scope, access rights, deployment and data flow, embeddedness and authority, governance and control, and organizational arrangement. The model is not the system; RAG is not a guarantee of truth; explainability is not interpretability; and responsible AI requires evidence and lifecycle controls. A manufacturing test shows why a closed generalpurpose API can suit bounded office work yet be a poor default for proprietary, operational or safety-critical tasks. Research limitations/implications: The framework is conceptual and requires validation across sectors, jurisdictions and use cases. Practical implications: Decision makers can use the framework to expose hidden dependencies, compare alternatives and connect debates about work, openness and sovereignty to system design. Originality: The contribution is a qualitative system-choice vector that joins architecture to authority, assurance, organizational dependence and effective control. It adds a ranked decision grammar and the "generality tax" hypothesis for strategic foresight.

title: Who Gains from AI? General-Equilibrium Rebound, Distribution, and Welfare *
affiliations: University of Copenhagen - Department of Economics

detail.title: Who Gains from AI? General-Equilibrium Rebound, Distribution, and Welfare *
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) can reduce labour required in individual tasks without reducing aggregate employment. This paper develops a static general-equilibrium model in which AI affects employment through lower user prices, demand-facing quality, complementary-task creation, wages, worker mobility, and AI-service costs. The model yields three main implications. First, conditional on factor prices, locally laboursaving AI can increase labour demand through demand expansion, quality improvement, and complementary-task creation. Labour-and AI-service-market adjustment then determine the associated equilibrium employment response. Second, aggregate employment growth need not benefit workers initially attached to exposed tasks: they may lose wages and employment while workers in complementary tasks gain. Third, employment growth is not a sufficient welfare criterion. Worker burden, unequal incidence, and AI-service rents can offset the real surplus created by the technology. The model also explains why occupational exposure alone cannot determine adoption or labour-market outcomes and identifies priorities for future empirical research.

title: Your Logo is a Toilet. Here is the Clinical Evidence.

detail.title: Your Logo is a Toilet. Here is the Clinical Evidence.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests and no personal or institutional relationships that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study because it did not involve human participants, patients, animals, clinical intervention, or identifiable personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding and was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a structural hypothesis about subconscious association risks embedded in the visual identities of BYD Group and its sub-brands Denza, Yangwang, and Fangchengbao. Drawing on gestalt psychology, cognitive priming theory, and the philosophical distinction between reductionist and emergent systems, the author argues that the identified marks fail to achieve emergent unity with the vehicles they identify — a property demonstrable by a simple ablation test: removing the mark changes the perceived vehicle not at all, whereas removing the badge from a Mercedes-Benz diminishes the whole. The paper documents, through a three-stage clinical association protocol, that the marks trigger unintended subconscious schemas — bathroom fixtures, personal care devices, sexual symbolism — before any product claim is processed. A control case (Mercedes-Benz three-pointed star) confirms the specificity of the finding: the same overlay protocol produces no gestalt closure for the control mark. The hypothesis is offered for empirical falsification through internal testing by the brand's own research team.

title: Email Marketing, Consumer Trust, and the AI Personalisation Frontier: Evidence from a Qualitative Rebranding Study

detail.title: Email Marketing, Consumer Trust, and the AI Personalisation Frontier: Evidence from a Qualitative Rebranding Study
detail.abstract:
This study examines the evolving role of rebranding in the digital age, particularly focusing on how email marketing can be an effective rebranding tool and how it shapes consumer perception. Based on a real-world rebranding experience at a UK-based digital marketing firm and qualitative data collected through semi-structured interviews with consumers and marketing professionals, three main objectives form this study: (1) understanding the evolving landscape of rebranding and its significance in organisations (2) aligning email marketing with rebranding objectives, and (3) offering recommendations for organisations navigating the digital era. The study also identifies the emergence of AI-driven personalisation as a strategic priority among organisations, and positions its psychological implications for consumer trust and autonomy as a pressing direction for future empirical inquiry. 

The findings indicate that personalisation and audience segmentation are key factors in an email during the rebranding stages. The findings further indicate that interactive content such as polls, surveys, and quizzes increases consumer engagement and strengthens consumer trust. A clear difference emerged between how organisations and consumers view email marketing. Organisations tend to focus on broader strategies and the use of new technologies, such as AI-powered personalisation, whereas consumers judge email marketing mainly by how relevant and valuable individual emails are to them. 

The study also highlights a growing interest among organisations in using AI for personalisation and automation, which is increasingly seen as the next stage in the evolution of email marketing. However, this shift raises important questions about consumer trust and autonomy, making it a valuable area for future research. 

While there are some limitations to the research, such as a small sample size and a focus on a single industry, it still offers valuable insights into how rebranding can strategically transform consumer perceptions with the help of email marketing. The research ultimately suggests that taking an integrated approach to rebranding is crucial, highlighting the significance of adaptability and innovation in today’s changing landscape.

title: Materialism in Consumer Finance and Related Research: Conceptual Foundations, Antecedents, Mechanisms, and Consequences
affiliations: University of Skovde - School of Business

detail.title: Materialism in Consumer Finance and Related Research: Conceptual Foundations, Antecedents, Mechanisms, and Consequences
detail.abstract: Materialism is not simply a preference for owning more. In consumer finance and related research, it has been treated as a value orientation, a cluster of personality tendencies, a set of extrinsic goals, and a means of constructing identity. This chapter traces those traditions and compares their principal measures, with particular attention to acquisition centrality, possession-defined success, happiness through ownership, status seeking, and identity signalling. It then examines how insecurity, selfesteem, family socialisation, peer comparison, media exposure, inequality, and market conditions foster materialistic orientations. The review links materialism to subjective and financial well-being, relationships, saving and spending, credit and debt, impulsive and compulsive buying, luxury consumption, and sustainable behaviour. These associations operate through impulsiveness, self-discrepancy, compensatory consumption, frustrated psychological needs, and social comparison, and are conditioned by self-control, mindfulness, financial capability, culture, socioeconomic position, and market institutions. Although the balance of evidence connects materialism with lower well-being, weaker financial security, and riskier consumption, the pattern is not uniform. Materialistic motives can also support planned acquisition or visible green and ethical consumption when such choices carry status or identity value. The chapter brings these findings together in a framework that distinguishes value-conflict from identity-signalling pathways and shows how motives and context shape their consequences.

title: Political Capture and Bureaucratic Behavior: Evidence from Mafia-Infiltrated Municipalities
affiliations: , Catholic University of the Sacred Heart of Milan, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart of Milan and Bocconi University

detail.title: Political Capture and Bureaucratic Behavior: Evidence from Mafia-Infiltrated Municipalities
detail.abstract: Local governments promise democratic responsiveness but are also vulnerable to political capture by illicit actors. While existing research documents the political and economic consequences of capture, less is known about how bureaucrats respond when political leadership is captured — whether they become instruments of corrupt rule or resist it. We examine these competing expectations in the context of Italian municipalities infiltrated by mafia organizations. Leveraging a law that allows the central government to dissolve captured municipal councils, we study how bureaucratic performance responds when political capture is abruptly removed. Using a difference-in-differences design with matched controls based on a machine-learning index of mafia-infiltration risk, we show that dissolutions substantially improve bureaucratic performance. Evidence from administrative data and investigative reports supports the interpretation that the lower performance during mafia rule was driven by bureaucrats resisting political capture. Our findings show that bureaucracies mitigate, rather than amplify, the downstream consequences of political capture.

title: Coal in Order to Reach Renewables: Carbon Capture, Synthetic Fuels, and the Atmospheric Ceiling
affiliations: and University of Toulouse 1 - Groupe de Recherche en Economie Mathématique et Quantitative (GREMAQ)

detail.title: Coal in Order to Reach Renewables: Carbon Capture, Synthetic Fuels, and the Atmospheric Ceiling
detail.abstract: We study the optimal use of energy from carbon emissions in an economy drawing useful energy from coal, a standard renewable, and methanol synthesised by combining captured CO2 with an otherwise inexploitable non-standard renewable, subject to a ceiling on atmospheric carbon. Captured CO2 carries a dual shadow value - atmospheric relief and productive feedstock - and we show that a credible ceiling is necessary and sufficient to activate the non-standard renewable: the ceiling, not any output subsidy, prices the feedstock that makes synthesis competitive. The optimal sequence departs from least-cost-first ordering, with coal and methanol used concurrently, and the pre-ceiling energy price may follow a U-shaped path driven by a rising shadow value rather than falling costs. A uniform Pigouvian carbon tax does not decentralise the optimum; a supplementary storage subsidy is required, and the net capture instrument is a subsidy or tax according to whether emission reduction dominates the coal rebound.
